```ts
  /** Grounds as the page prints them. */
  grounds: {
    force_majeure: "force majeure",
    manifest_error: "manifest error",
    insufficient_information: "insufficient information",
    withdrawn: "withdrawn",
    annulled: "annulled",
    scrutiny: "after scrutiny",
    not_authentic: "not authentic",
    wrong_item: "wrong item",
  } as Record<string, string>,
  /** A figure the rows can no longer give, as tco-counts prints it: never 0. */
  notRecorded: "not recorded",
  ordersHeld: "Orders that an authority's decision forbids korbat to disclose are counted after that decision ends. A year can gain a second, marked version for that reason.",
  recipientsHeading: "Recipients",
  recipients: (month: string, low: string, high: string) =>
    `Average monthly active recipients of korbat (Article 24(2) of the Digital Services Act), over the six months to ${month}: between ${low} and ${high}.`,
  recipientsOff: (month: string, low: string) =>
    `Average monthly active recipients of korbat (Article 24(2) of the Digital Services Act), over the six months to ${month}: at least ${low}; korbat does not count readers without an account.`,
  recipientsNotYet: "korbat has not counted six full months yet.",
  method: (method: number) =>
    `How korbat counts (method ${method}). An account that was used while signed in during a month is counted once for that month. A reader without an account is counted once for each day they read korbat: korbat cannot tell whether Tuesday's reader is Monday's, because it keeps nothing that could tell. So the true number lies between the first figure, accounts alone, and the second, accounts plus the sum of each day's readers. To count, korbat feeds a counting sketch: a small summary that cannot list who was counted. For a reader without an account it is fed with a keyed digest of the network address and the browser's name, under a random key that exists for ${RECIPIENT_RULES.saltHours} hours in korbat's short-lived store and is written nowhere else. Until a month's sketch is deleted at the month's end, whoever runs korbat's server could still ask it whether one given account was probably counted in that month; after that korbat keeps two numbers and nothing else. A crawler is left out only when it names itself. korbat does not record where a reader is, so readers outside the European Union are counted too.`,
  // The audit log's daily value (3d Task 5; 9.3 item 6, W.2).
  headHeading: "The audit log's daily value",
  head: "Each day korbat publishes one value computed from the day and the newest entry of its staff audit log, the record of everything korbat's staff confirm with their keys. If an earlier entry were changed or removed later, the log would no longer lead to the values published since. A value shows neither how many entries the log has nor any entry, and it differs from one day to the next also when nothing was added to the log. A value on korbat's own page proves nothing against korbat's operator, who could change this page too: so the same value goes each day to a person who does not run the server, and, when the outside timestamp is on, to a timestamp authority.",
  /** A day's row: its value, and who witnessed it ("witness" reads none for a row without a token). */
  headRow: (day: string, value: string, witness: HeadWitness) => `${day}: ${value}, ${HEAD_WITNESS_WORDS[witness]}`,
  /** [tr.headMissing], in the row of a day between two shown days that has no value. */
  headMissingRow: (day: string) => `${day}: no value was published`,
  /** [tr.restore], a restore's row; the second sentence names the newest value above it that still fits, or says none does. */
  restore: (day: string, lastDay: string | null) =>
    `${day}: korbat restored its database from a backup. ${lastDay === null ? "No value above still fits the restored log." : `The newest value above that still fits the restored log is of ${lastDay}.`}`,
  /** [tr.retired], after a retired value. */
  retired: (day: string) => `retired by the restore of ${day}: true when published, and fits no log now`,
  /**
   * [tr.verify], while a shown row has a proof, with the newest such day's value and file: the command as it was run once
   * against a proof of a local test authority (OpenSSL 3.5.4), where it answered "Verification: OK" for the value and
   * failed for another value and for another authority's certificates.
   */
  verify: (value: string, day: string) =>
    `To check a day: download its proof, get the timestamp authority's certificates from the authority itself, and run: openssl ts -verify -digest ${value} -in ${day}.tsr -CAfile <certificates>. It answers "Verification: OK" when that authority signed this value at the time the proof states.`,
  download: (day: string) => `Download the proof of ${day} (${day}.tsr)`,
  headNone: "korbat has published no daily value yet.",
  tdbHeading: "The Transparency Database",
  tdb: "korbat does not send its statements of reasons to the European Commission's DSA Transparency Database. That duty (Article 24(5) of the Digital Services Act) does not apply to micro and small enterprises (Article 19(1)), which korbat is, and a statement sent there cannot be taken back. Should korbat outgrow the exemption, this page will say from which day it sends them.",
  rulesLink: "The rules",
  exploreLink: "How Explore works",
} as const;
```

### Replace `infra/.env.example` (whole file)

```text
# Copy to infra/.env and change every password. Never commit infra/.env.
POSTGRES_USER=postgres
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=change-me-superuser
POSTGRES_DB=korbat
KORBAT_MIGRATE_DB_PASSWORD=change-me-migrate
KORBAT_API_DB_PASSWORD=change-me-api
KORBAT_AUTH_DB_PASSWORD=change-me-auth
# The database role of the contact point's watcher, notify (3f). infra/postgres/init/01-roles.sh makes it on a new data
# directory; on one that exists the README's Upgrading makes it once. notify's own settings are below, under 3f.
KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD=change-me-notify
# Valkey (the session cache and rate-limit counters) refuses every command without it.
REDIS_PASSWORD=change-me-redis

# Images. The formats korbat accepts: remove one to refuse it and keep its decoder blocked, for
# example after a security advisory against that decoder, then restart api and worker.
MEDIA_FORMATS=jpeg,png,webp,gif,avif
# Uploads are refused while a media volume has less free space than this many bytes (2 GiB). The
# volumes share a disk with Postgres, and a full disk stops the database.
MEDIA_MIN_FREE_BYTES=2147483648
# The sweeper's pass that deletes images without a database row: on refuses when there are many of
# them (a database restored from an older snapshot looks like that), off skips it during a restore,
# force deletes them once you have checked.
MEDIA_RECONCILE=on

API_LOG_LEVEL=info
# Comma-separated browser origins allowed to call the API cross-origin. Empty in prod (same origin via Caddy).
API_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:8081

# Auth. `node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` fills the keys with random values and shares them with apps/api/.env.
# Origin the web app is served from (Caddy). Production: https://<your domain>.
API_APP_ORIGIN=http://localhost:8080
# Which header names the client: cloudflare when the tunnel is the only way in (the API then trusts
# cf-connecting-ip), caddy when Caddy's port is reachable directly. Never none behind a proxy.
API_TRUST_PROXY=caddy
API_AUTH_HMAC_KEY=change-me-key-auth-hmac
API_IP_HASH_KEY=change-me-key-ip-hash
API_TOTP_ENC_KEY=v1:change-me-key-totp
# Earlier TOTP keys, comma-separated, kept only while secrets they encrypted are still stored; a secret
# read with one is re-encrypted with API_TOTP_ENC_KEY.
API_TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS=
# Encrypts what a signed-out notifier leaves to be told about their notice: a name, an address and the token of the
# mails' link. Keep it secret and backed up as API_TOTP_ENC_KEY is: without it korbat can neither mail a notifier nor
# say who sent a notice.
API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY=v1:change-me-key-notifier
# Earlier notifier keys, comma-separated. A contact is never encrypted again, so a key stays here while a contact it
# encrypted is still stored.
API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS=
# Cloudflare's documented always-pass test secret. Production uses the secret of your Turnstile widget.
API_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY=1x0000000000000000000000000000000AA
# Mailpit from compose.dev.yml. Production: the EU relay, e.g. smtps://user:pass@smtp-relay.example:465
API_SMTP_URL=smtp://mailpit:1025
API_MAIL_FROM="korbat <no-reply@korbat.local>"
API_TERMS_VERSION=draft-2026-09
# Who checks the phone number behind the verified badge: off turns the badge off, dev accepts the code
# 000000 (development only; production refuses it), vonage texts a real code through Vonage Verify with the
# key and secret from the Vonage dashboard (the runbook in the 1b design says how).
API_VERIFY_PROVIDER=off
# Whether the web app's account settings show the verified badge section: on or off. Set it together with
# API_VERIFY_PROVIDER: off while that is off, on once it is dev or vonage (a section shown without a provider
# answers every Send code with "Verification is not available"). The web image reads it as EXPO_PUBLIC_BADGE,
# which Expo inlines at export time.
WEB_BADGE=off
API_VONAGE_API_KEY=
API_VONAGE_API_SECRET=
# The sender name of the verification text: 1 to 18 characters, none of / { } : $.
API_VERIFY_BRAND=korbat
# Passkeys. The RP ID every passkey is bound to: empty means the host of API_APP_ORIGIN. It may instead be a parent
# domain of that host (korbat.example for app.korbat.example). The staff console does not use it: staff keys have their
# own RP ID. Production refuses an IP address or localhost. Choose it before the first passkey is added: changing it
# later strands every passkey.
API_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID=
# The site name password managers show next to a korbat passkey: 1 to 64 printable characters; empty means korbat.
API_WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME=

# The staff console: the origin staff open it at, served by Caddy's second site (port 8090 in its container). Empty
# switches the console off: every /api/staff path then answers 404. It must differ from API_APP_ORIGIN and never appear
# in API_TRUSTED_ORIGINS. In development it is localhost on the port compose.dev.yml publishes the console on
# (DEV_CONSOLE_PORT below); open it there, never at 127.0.0.1. Production: https://<the console's own hostname>, a
# hostname apart from the app's.
API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN=http://localhost:8090
# The RP ID staff keys are bound to: empty means the hostname of API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN, which production requires. Choose
# the console's hostname before the first staff key is enrolled: moving the console later means enrolling every key
# again.
API_CONSOLE_RP_ID=

# Moderation. The hour of the UTC day, 0 to 23, at which the day's decisions on reports and notices are released to those
# who sent them, in one batch, so that nobody can tell from a mail's minute when a decision was made; empty means 7.
API_MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR=7
# The queue's emergency switch, published in the terms: on sorts cases whose open reports all come from unproven sources
# after the others of their lane, never below a less severe lane. off, the default, orders by lane and age alone.
API_MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN=off
# The retention job, which erases what is due and deletes kept image rows that nothing retains any more: on unless set
# to off. While it is off nothing is erased or deleted, the API logs a warning at every start, and the console counts
# what is late. off only for a restore window: README, Restoring, step 5
API_MODERATION_RETENTION=on

# Authorities' orders and the alert channel (3f). Whether the API judges the alert channel's health: on mails "Phone
# alerts are down" when the watcher's beat or a push is late; off (the default outside production) only skips that
# check, and the console's home says that phone alerts are switched off on this server. Leave it off until the
# contact-point mailbox exists (README, Upgrading).
API_NOTIFY=off
# The operator's Member State, as an ISO code of a state whose facts the contracts hold (Germany's, DE, is the worked
# example), from which the console tells an order from another Member State; and the published contact point for
# authorities, an address. Leave the contact point empty until the owner's list is done (README, Before going public):
# the home state is required once it is set. The migrate service reads the home state too, for staff.js order-open.
API_HOME_STATE=DE
API_CONTACT_POINT=
# The report hold (3f): while a report of an account's sealed images to the authorities is owed, a deletion of the
# account keeps its email address, and nothing else of it, for at most seven days, and its deletion mail says so. on is
# the default; off restores the purge that overwrites the address at once, and then a report needs the address taken
# before the account is deleted (README, Notifications and hand-overs).
API_REPORT_HOLD=on
# The edge's purge (3d): when an image stops being public, the API asks the network provider to drop its copies at the
# edge, by prefix, several images a request. off (the default) asks nothing, and the image's header is then
# the only bound on a copy. test is for the suites and is refused while APP_SITE is open. cloudflare needs the zone's
# id, an API token with the one permission Zone, Cache Purge (a secret: keep it as the keys above are, and it is in no
# log line), and the public hostname images are served under, without a scheme or a path (README, The edge).
API_EDGE_PURGE=off
API_EDGE_ZONE_ID=
API_EDGE_API_TOKEN=
API_EDGE_HOST=
# The recipients' count (3d): the transparency page and staff.js recipients count the accounts used each month and,
# while this is on, the readers without an account each day, by a keyed digest of the network and the browser's name
# under a random key that lives 26 hours and is written nowhere else. on is the default; off leaves readers without an
# account out, and the pages then say "at least" (README, The yearly edition).
API_RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT=on
# The audit head's daily value (3d): once a day after the dispatch hour the API publishes it on /transparency and mails
# it, with its place and hash, to the keeper's address below, the staff member who does not run the server; empty sends
# no mail. Its outside timestamp: off (the default), test (for the suites, refused while APP_SITE is open), or rfc3161
# with the https address of a timestamp authority the owner has chosen, which is sent the day's value and nothing else
# (README, The yearly edition).
API_HEAD_WITNESS=off
API_HEAD_WITNESS_URL=
API_HEAD_KEEPER_MAIL=
# The R1 check (3d), read by the worker and the API, so unprefixed: off (the default) rates no image, and R1 stays
# report-driven; test is for the suites and is refused while APP_SITE is open; onnx, a real classifier, is not in this
# build and stops both at start.
R1_CLASSIFIER=off
# Whether a score over the threshold also withholds its image until a person decides (on), or only opens a finding for a
# moderator (off, the default). The day of the owner's impact assessment for the check, and the day it covered the
# withhold: a real classifier needs the first, and its withhold the second; /rules prints both.
API_AUTOMATION_R1_ACTS=off
API_AUTOMATION_DPIA_R1=
API_AUTOMATION_DPIA_R1_ACTS=
# The comparison of uploads with known material (3d), unprefixed: off (the default) computes no fingerprint and compares
# nothing; test is for the suites and is refused while APP_SITE is open; a source's name needs that source's adapter,
# which this build does not carry, and stops the API at start. Whether an acting match on a post also seals its images
# until an admin answers (on, the default once a comparison runs) or only raises the urgent item (off). The day of the
# owner's impact assessment for the comparison, and the day it covered the seal: a real source needs the first, and its
# seal the second; /rules prints both.
MEDIA_MATCH=off
API_AUTOMATION_R2_ACTS=on
API_AUTOMATION_DPIA_MATCH=
API_AUTOMATION_DPIA_MATCH_ACTS=
# The watcher and the push server run under the Compose profile notify, switched on here once the mailbox and the phones
# exist: COMPOSE_PROFILES=notify. Nothing below is needed for the stack to start while it is off. The mailbox: IMAP over
# TLS on port 993, an application password that can only read, and the name of the junk folder as the mail host names it.
# The publisher's ntfy token is also in infra/ntfy/server.yml; production refuses the example's.
# COMPOSE_PROFILES=notify
# NOTIFY_IMAP_HOST=
# NOTIFY_IMAP_USER=
# NOTIFY_IMAP_PASSWORD=
# NOTIFY_IMAP_JUNK=Junk
# NTFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN=
# The push network's fixed subnet, which the app's and the console's sites refuse; Caddy is on that network with
# the profile off too. The default lies outside the pools Docker gives its own networks (172.17.0.0/16 to 172.31.0.0/16,
# and 192.168.0.0/16): set another only if this host's own network uses it.
# PUSH_SUBNET=172.16.91.0/24
# The watcher's fixed address on that network, which infra/ntfy/server.yml exempts from ntfy's request limit
# (visitor-request-limit-exempt-hosts): with another subnet, set an address inside it here and in that file's line.
# NOTIFY_PUSH_IP=172.16.91.254

# The app's site (3f): open, or closed while a restored database is checked, when it answers 503 to every path, the
# API's included; the console's site stays open. Caddy reads it when it starts and refuses to start on any other value.
# The API reads it too (3d), when it starts: it refuses a test adapter while the site is open.
APP_SITE=open

# Public Turnstile site key baked into the web image. Cloudflare's always-pass test key for development;
# production uses the site key of the same widget as API_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY.
WEB_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY=1x00000000000000000000AA
# The address people write to when the report form does not work for them, to ask for their data, or about a decision.
# It is baked into the web image as EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_EMAIL: the report form names it when the human check fails or
# the limits are reached, and the terms page shows it. The image refuses to build without an address, and a
# production build refuses a placeholder (a domain ending in .local, .localhost, .test, .invalid or .example, or
# example.com, example.org or example.net). A person reads this mailbox every working day.
WEB_CONTACT_EMAIL=contact@korbat.local
# 3f: the contact point for authorities and the Member State korbat is established in, baked into the web image as
# EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT and EXPO_PUBLIC_HOME_STATE for the terms' sections on them: the page cannot read the API's
# API_CONTACT_POINT and API_HOME_STATE, which hold the same two values. The terms print the contact point only while it
# is set, and the image refuses a point without its state. Set both, with the API's, as the last step of the README's
# Before going public, then rebuild the caddy service.
WEB_CONTACT_POINT=
WEB_HOME_STATE=DE

# development or production. It is the API's NODE_ENV (production refuses Turnstile test keys, plain-http
# origins and a relay without TLS) and a build argument of the web image (production refuses the
# Turnstile test site key). Set it to production before building the images for the public.
KORBAT_ENV=development
# on when cloudflared is the only way in: Caddy then keeps CF-Connecting-IP for the API (and
# API_TRUST_PROXY is cloudflare). off drops the header, so nobody on the network can claim an address.
TUNNEL=off
# Cloudflare Tunnel token (Zero Trust > Networks > Tunnels). Only needed with --profile tunnel. The
# tunnel has three public hostnames: the app's, pointing at http://caddy:8080, the staff console's (the hostname of
# API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN), pointing at http://caddy:8090, and the phones' push hostname (3f), pointing at
# http://caddy:8091. Leave the HTTP Host Header setting of each empty, so the API sees the hostname the browser used.
TUNNEL_TOKEN=

# The development stack's host ports, read only by infra/compose.dev.yml. Set one when another container
# on this machine holds the default, and give apps/api/.env the same port. Defaults: 55432, 56379, 3000,
# 8080, 8090, 51025, 58025, 8091, 2586.
# DEV_PG_PORT=55432
# DEV_REDIS_PORT=56379
# DEV_API_PORT=3000
# DEV_CADDY_PORT=8080
# The staff console's port: API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN must name the same port on localhost (http://localhost:<port>).
# DEV_CONSOLE_PORT=8090
# DEV_SMTP_PORT=51025
# DEV_MAILPIT_PORT=58025
# 3f, with the profile notify: the push site, which a test client subscribes through, and ntfy's own port, which only
# `pnpm --filter @korbat/api notify:dev` publishes to (NOTIFY_PUSH_URL in apps/api/.env).
# DEV_PUSH_PORT=8091
# DEV_NTFY_PORT=2586
```

### Replace `infra/compose.yml` (whole file)

```yaml
name: korbat

x-logging: &logging
  driver: json-file
  options: { max-size: "20m", max-file: "5" }

x-node-common: &node-common
  restart: unless-stopped
  read_only: true
  tmpfs: ["/tmp"]
  security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
  logging: *logging

services:
  postgres:
    # PostgreSQL 18. From 18 on the image keeps the cluster under /var/lib/postgresql/<major>/docker, so
    # the volume is mounted one level up and a later major can pg_upgrade inside it. A cluster from the
    # earlier pgdata volume (PostgreSQL 16) is moved over by scripts/pg-major-upgrade.mjs.
    image: postgres:18.6-alpine@sha256:77f585114c32fbca283dc835b0596f4e52b51b4c6662d7810b2f4084f60a1873
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 1g
    memswap_limit: 1g
    pids_limit: 256
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB}
      KORBAT_MIGRATE_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_MIGRATE_DB_PASSWORD}
      KORBAT_API_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_API_DB_PASSWORD}
      KORBAT_AUTH_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_AUTH_DB_PASSWORD}
      # The contact point's watcher's role (3f), which 01-roles.sh makes on a new data directory. Not required: a stack
      # without the watcher runs without it.
      KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD:-}
    volumes:
      - pgdata18:/var/lib/postgresql
      - ./postgres/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
    # watch: the watcher's own network to the database, which holds nothing else.
    networks: [data, watch]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER} -d ${POSTGRES_DB}"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  redis:
    # Valkey, the BSD-licensed fork of Redis, under the service name the URLs already use. A password
    # is required: nothing on the data network may read the session cache without it.
    image: valkey/valkey:9.1.2-alpine@sha256:48332870af354a799964c0012ae1194a0bf2bf894eb508f945810596dc2d8d11
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 384m
    memswap_limit: 384m
    pids_limit: 64
    environment:
      REDIS_PASSWORD: ${REDIS_PASSWORD:?set REDIS_PASSWORD in infra/.env}
    command: ["sh", "-c", "exec valkey-server --appendonly yes --maxmemory 256mb --maxmemory-policy noeviction --requirepass $$REDIS_PASSWORD"]
    volumes:
    # A fresh volume: Valkey 9 cannot read the RDB format 12 that Redis 7.4 wrote into `redisdata`, and that
    # volume held only transient state (limits, codes in flight, cached sessions, queued image jobs).
      - valkeydata:/data
    networks: [data]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "VALKEYCLI_AUTH=$$REDIS_PASSWORD valkey-cli ping | grep -q PONG"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  migrate:
    <<: *node-common
    restart: "no"
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: apps/api/Dockerfile
    command: ["node", "dist/migrate.js"]
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: postgres://korbat_migrate:${KORBAT_MIGRATE_DB_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
      MIGRATIONS_DIR: /app/migrations
      # `staff.js enroll` runs here, as the migrator, the one role the running API never holds, and records on each link
      # the console's origin and relying party ID it is issued for. Empty, the console is off and enroll refuses.
      CONSOLE_ORIGIN: ${API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN:-}
      CONSOLE_RP_ID: ${API_CONSOLE_RP_ID:-}
      # 3f: staff.js order-open runs here too, and reads the home state (whether an order is cross-border) and the app's
      # origin (how a link is read, as the console's route reads it). Neither is required: enroll and the migrations run
      # without them, and order-open refuses with one sentence while either is empty.
      HOME_STATE: ${API_HOME_STATE:-}
      APP_ORIGIN: ${API_APP_ORIGIN:-}
    networks: [data]
    depends_on:
      postgres: { condition: service_healthy }

  api:
    <<: *node-common
    # The image's name, the one Compose gives it by default, written out: notify (3f) runs the same image, so it is
    # built once.
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: apps/api/Dockerfile
      args:
        KORBAT_VERSION: ${KORBAT_VERSION:-0.0.0}
    mem_limit: 512m
    memswap_limit: 512m
    pids_limit: 256
    environment:
      # development or production, from infra/.env; production turns on the guards against test keys, plain-http
      # origins and a relay without TLS. The worker below always runs as production.
      NODE_ENV: ${KORBAT_ENV:?set KORBAT_ENV to development or production in infra/.env}
      PORT: "3000"
      LOG_LEVEL: ${API_LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      DATABASE_URL_API: postgres://korbat_api:${KORBAT_API_DB_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
      DATABASE_URL_AUTH: postgres://korbat_auth:${KORBAT_AUTH_DB_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
      REDIS_URL: redis://:${REDIS_PASSWORD}@redis:6379
      TRUSTED_ORIGINS: ${API_TRUSTED_ORIGINS:-}
      # Which header names the client: the stack refuses to start without a choice.
      TRUST_PROXY: ${API_TRUST_PROXY:?set API_TRUST_PROXY in infra/.env}
      # Auth settings. The stack refuses to start while any of these is missing from infra/.env.
      APP_ORIGIN: ${API_APP_ORIGIN:?set API_APP_ORIGIN in infra/.env}
      AUTH_HMAC_KEY: ${API_AUTH_HMAC_KEY:?set API_AUTH_HMAC_KEY in infra/.env}
      IP_HASH_KEY: ${API_IP_HASH_KEY:?set API_IP_HASH_KEY in infra/.env}
      TOTP_ENC_KEY: ${API_TOTP_ENC_KEY:?set API_TOTP_ENC_KEY in infra/.env}
      TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS: ${API_TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS:-}
      # Encrypts a signed-out notifier's name and address; earlier keys stay accepted for decryption.
      NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY: ${API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY:?set API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY in infra/.env}
      NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS: ${API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS:-}
      TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY: ${API_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY:?set API_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY in infra/.env}
      SMTP_URL: ${API_SMTP_URL:?set API_SMTP_URL in infra/.env}
      MAIL_FROM: ${API_MAIL_FROM:?set API_MAIL_FROM in infra/.env}
      TERMS_VERSION: ${API_TERMS_VERSION:?set API_TERMS_VERSION in infra/.env}
      # The verified badge's phone check. off (the default) hides the badge; vonage needs the two credentials.
      VERIFY_PROVIDER: ${API_VERIFY_PROVIDER:-off}
      VONAGE_API_KEY: ${API_VONAGE_API_KEY:-}
      VONAGE_API_SECRET: ${API_VONAGE_API_SECRET:-}
      VERIFY_BRAND: ${API_VERIFY_BRAND:-korbat}
      # Passkeys. Empty values leave the API's defaults: the host of APP_ORIGIN as the RP ID and korbat as the name.
      WEBAUTHN_RP_ID: ${API_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID:-}
      WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME: ${API_WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME:-}
      # The staff console, served by Caddy's second site: the origin staff open it at, and the RP ID staff keys are bound
      # to (empty means the console's hostname). An empty origin switches the console off: every /api/staff path then
      # answers 404. The migrate service gets the same two values for `staff.js enroll`.
      CONSOLE_ORIGIN: ${API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN:-}
      CONSOLE_RP_ID: ${API_CONSOLE_RP_ID:-}
      # Moderation: the UTC hour of the daily release of decisions to those who reported, the queue's emergency switch, and
      # the retention job's switch, which is off only for a restore window (README, Restoring, step 5).
      MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR: ${API_MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR:-7}
      MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN: ${API_MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN:-off}
      MODERATION_RETENTION: ${API_MODERATION_RETENTION:-on}
      # Authorities' orders (3f): whether the alert tick judges the alert channel's health. Empty means on in production;
      # off until the contact point's mailbox exists (README, Upgrading).
      NOTIFY: ${API_NOTIFY:-}
      # The operator's Member State, a state whose facts the contracts hold (DE is filled in), and the published contact
      # point for authorities. Both empty until the owner's list is done; the home state is required once the contact
      # point is set.
      HOME_STATE: ${API_HOME_STATE:-}
      CONTACT_POINT: ${API_CONTACT_POINT:-}
      # 3f Task 5: whether a deletion keeps an account's address, at most seven days, while a report of its sealed images
      # to the authorities is owed. Empty means on; off restores the purge that overwrites the address at once.
      REPORT_HOLD: ${API_REPORT_HOLD:-}
      # 3d: the app's site switch, Caddy's (3f), handed to the API too, which refuses a test adapter while the site is open.
      APP_SITE: ${APP_SITE:-open}
      # 3d Task 3: the purge of an image's copies at the edge once it stops being public: off (empty, the default), test
      # (refused while APP_SITE is open) or cloudflare, which needs the zone's id, the API token with the one permission
      # Zone, Cache Purge, and the public hostname images are served under (README, The edge).
      EDGE_PURGE: ${API_EDGE_PURGE:-}
      EDGE_ZONE_ID: ${API_EDGE_ZONE_ID:-}
      EDGE_API_TOKEN: ${API_EDGE_API_TOKEN:-}
      EDGE_HOST: ${API_EDGE_HOST:-}
      # 3d Task 4: whether readers without an account are counted among the recipients, each day's by a keyed digest of
      # the network and the browser's name under a salt that lives 26 hours; on unless set to off (README, The yearly edition).
      RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT: ${API_RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT:-}
      # 3d Task 5: the audit head's daily value. Its outside timestamp: off (empty, the default), test (refused while
      # APP_SITE is open) or rfc3161, which needs the timestamp authority's https address; and the one address the
      # keeper's daily mail goes to, empty for none (README, The yearly edition).
      HEAD_WITNESS: ${API_HEAD_WITNESS:-}
      HEAD_WITNESS_URL: ${API_HEAD_WITNESS_URL:-}
      HEAD_KEEPER_MAIL: ${API_HEAD_KEEPER_MAIL:-}
      # 3d Task 6: the R1 check, which the worker reads too (unprefixed): off (empty, the default), test (refused while
      # APP_SITE is open) or onnx, not in this build; whether a score over the threshold withholds its image (off unless
      # on); and the two days of the owner's impact assessment, empty for none.
      R1_CLASSIFIER: ${R1_CLASSIFIER:-}
      AUTOMATION_R1_ACTS: ${API_AUTOMATION_R1_ACTS:-}
      AUTOMATION_DPIA_R1: ${API_AUTOMATION_DPIA_R1:-}
      AUTOMATION_DPIA_R1_ACTS: ${API_AUTOMATION_DPIA_R1_ACTS:-}
      # 3d Task 7: the comparison of uploads with known material (unprefixed, as the design names it beside R1_CLASSIFIER):
      # off (empty, the default), test (refused while APP_SITE is open) or a source's name, which no adapter of this build
      # answers; whether an acting match on a post seals its images (on unless off); and its two days, empty for none. The
      # worker is not handed it: it computes no perceptual hash in this build.
      MEDIA_MATCH: ${MEDIA_MATCH:-}
      AUTOMATION_R2_ACTS: ${API_AUTOMATION_R2_ACTS:-}
      AUTOMATION_DPIA_MATCH: ${API_AUTOMATION_DPIA_MATCH:-}
      AUTOMATION_DPIA_MATCH_ACTS: ${API_AUTOMATION_DPIA_MATCH_ACTS:-}
      # Images. The API writes uploads and only reads what the worker stored.
      MEDIA_UPLOADS_DIR: /media/uploads
      MEDIA_STORE_DIR: /media/store
      MEDIA_FORMATS: ${MEDIA_FORMATS:-jpeg,png,webp,gif,avif}
      MEDIA_MIN_FREE_BYTES: ${MEDIA_MIN_FREE_BYTES:-2147483648}
      MEDIA_RECONCILE: ${MEDIA_RECONCILE:-on}
    volumes:
      - media-uploads:/media/uploads
      - media-store:/media/store:ro
    networks: [app, data]
    depends_on:
      migrate: { condition: service_completed_successfully }
      redis: { condition: service_healthy }
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/health"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10

  # The image worker runs the decoder, the most exploitable code in the stack. It has no network at
  # all, no credentials and no capabilities: it reads uploads and writes the store, and that is
  # everything it can reach. The memory limit was sized on worst-case images (2b design, Research).
  worker:
    <<: *node-common
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: apps/worker/Dockerfile
    network_mode: none
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    mem_limit: 768m
    memswap_limit: 768m
    cpus: 1.0
    pids_limit: 64
    tmpfs: ["/tmp:size=64m"]
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      LOG_LEVEL: ${API_LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      MEDIA_UPLOADS_DIR: /media/uploads
      MEDIA_STORE_DIR: /media/store
      MEDIA_FORMATS: ${MEDIA_FORMATS:-jpeg,png,webp,gif,avif}
      # 3d Task 6: the R1 check's scorer, the API's setting (off when empty), and the site's switch, which the worker reads
      # only to refuse a test scorer while the site is open.
      R1_CLASSIFIER: ${R1_CLASSIFIER:-}
      APP_SITE: ${APP_SITE:-open}
    volumes:
      - media-uploads:/media/uploads:ro
      - media-store:/media/store
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "node", "-e", "process.exit(Date.now() - JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('/media/store/heartbeat', 'utf8')).at < 60000 ? 0 : 1)"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 4

  # The contact point's watcher (3f design, section 5): the API's image with dist/notify.js, under the profile notify. It
  # reads the contact-point mailbox over IMAP and publishes the alerts to ntfy. On the network watch it reaches PostgreSQL
  # as korbat_notify, whose grants are four tables, and nothing else; on push it reaches ntfy. It never joins data, where
  # the API listens and the limit store is. It exits rather than hang, and Docker starts it again. No setting of it is
  # required by Compose: the program names the one it is missing and exits.
  notify:
    <<: *node-common
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    profiles: ["notify"]
    command: ["node", "dist/notify.js"]
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    # Measured in this image (3f Task 1): about 82 MB resident idle, a peak of 93 MB during a first read of 10,000 old
    # messages, which took 21 seconds and fell back to 81 MB; under this limit the container's peak was 85 MB, with no
    # kill. 128 MB keeps more than a third above that peak.
    mem_limit: 128m
    memswap_limit: 128m
    pids_limit: 64
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: ${KORBAT_ENV:-production}
      LOG_LEVEL: ${API_LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      DATABASE_URL_NOTIFY: postgres://korbat_notify:${KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD:-}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_HOST: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_HOST:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_USER: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_USER:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_PASSWORD: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_PASSWORD:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_JUNK: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_JUNK:-}
      NTFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN: ${NTFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN:-}
    # A fixed address on push (3f's review, operations3), which infra/ntfy/server.yml exempts from ntfy's request limit
    # (visitor-request-limit-exempt-hosts): ntfy lets any one address publish 60 times and then once every 5 seconds (lab
    # L1), which would hold an order's alert behind a flood of contact mail. It lies inside PUSH_SUBNET, at the top of
    # the range, which Docker hands out last; change it, and the file's line, with the subnet.
    networks:
      watch: {}
      push:
        ipv4_address: ${NOTIFY_PUSH_IP:-172.16.91.254}
    depends_on:
      migrate: { condition: service_completed_successfully }
      ntfy: { condition: service_started }
    # The watcher writes the time of every round it ends; two minutes without one is a hang.
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "node", "-e", "process.exit(Date.now() - Number(require('fs').readFileSync('/tmp/korbat-notify-beat', 'utf8')) < 120000 ? 0 : 1)"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s

  # The hand-over of one seal's files (3f design, sections 5 and 7.14), under the profile handover, started by the operator
  # alone: docker compose --profile handover run --rm -T -v <directory>:/handover handover < list > digests. The API's
  # image with dist/handover.js, which opens no database and no socket: no network at all, no credential, no capability,
  # the image store and (3d) the quarantine read-only, the quarantine looked in first. It has no bind mount here: the
  # directory for the archive is an argument of the command (an empty source would stop every Compose command of the
  # stack), on an encrypted volume owned by uid 1000, the image's user node, the only place it can write. No setting of
  # it is required.
  handover:
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    profiles: ["handover"]
    command: ["node", "dist/handover.js"]
    restart: "no"
    network_mode: none
    read_only: true
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    tmpfs: ["/tmp"]
    stdin_open: true
    volumes:
      - media-store:/media/store:ro
      - media-quarantine:/media/quarantine:ro

  # The quarantine's mover (3d design, sections 5 and 7.1), under the profile quarantine, started by the operator alone:
  # docker compose -f infra/compose.yml --profile quarantine run --rm -T quarantine < list > receipt, with the list that
  # staff.js quarantine-list printed, and the receipt then recorded by staff.js quarantine-record (the README,
  # Quarantine). The API's image with dist/quarantine.js, which opens no database and no socket: no network at all, no
  # environment, no credential, no capability and a read-only root; the image store and the quarantine read-write, and
  # nothing else. Its two roots are arguments of its entry point, and it refuses to start without both; what follows the
  # service's name on the command line (--lost, --inventory) is appended to them. It is the one service that writes the
  # quarantine; handover reads it, and the api, migrate and worker services never mount it.

    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    profiles: ["quarantine"]
    entrypoint: ["node", "dist/quarantine.js", "/media/store", "/media/quarantine"]
    restart: "no"
    network_mode: none
    read_only: true
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    stdin_open: true
    volumes:
      - media-store:/media/store
      - media-quarantine:/media/quarantine

  # The push server (3f design, section 5), under the profile notify, never linked into korbat's programs: ntfy at its
  # pinned release, reading its users, rights and tokens from infra/ntfy/server.yml (git-ignored, made from
  # server.yml.example), mounted read-only, since Compose would blank the $2a$10$ of a password hash in a variable. Only
  # on push, which is internal: it has no route out, so nothing is forwarded upstream. Its cache and auth files are on its
  # volume, at /var/tmp, the one directory of the image its user may write to.
  ntfy:
    image: binwiederhier/ntfy:v2.28.0@sha256:6ef4b819f722fccdc036af611c4774cfdc2de821ab74fdd48bbf4c9d6f8973da
    profiles: ["notify"]
    command: ["serve", "--config", "/etc/ntfy/server.yml"]
    restart: unless-stopped
    read_only: true
    user: "1000:1000"
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 128m
    memswap_limit: 128m
    pids_limit: 64
    volumes:
      - ./ntfy/server.yml:/etc/ntfy/server.yml:ro
      - ntfy-data:/var/tmp
    networks: [push]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://127.0.0.1:2586/v1/health"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 4

  # Caddy serves the web app on port 8080, proxying /api, the staff console on port 8090, proxying only /api/staff, and
  # (3f) the phones' push site on port 8091, proxying only the two topics' subscriptions to ntfy. It runs as its own
  # user, sees only the API and ntfy, and is the only thing cloudflared can reach. A client from the push network (ntfy,
  # the watcher) is refused 403 on the app's and the console's sites.
  caddy:
    restart: unless-stopped
    read_only: true
    tmpfs: ["/tmp"]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 128m
    memswap_limit: 128m
    pids_limit: 64
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: infra/caddy/Dockerfile
      args:
        EXPO_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY: ${WEB_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY:?set WEB_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY in infra/.env}
        KORBAT_ENV: ${KORBAT_ENV:?set KORBAT_ENV to development or production in infra/.env}
        TUNNEL: ${TUNNEL:-off}
        EXPO_PUBLIC_BADGE: ${WEB_BADGE:-off}
        EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_EMAIL: ${WEB_CONTACT_EMAIL:?set WEB_CONTACT_EMAIL in infra/.env}
        # 3f: the terms' contact point for authorities and korbat's Member State; neither is required (Before going public).
        EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT: ${WEB_CONTACT_POINT:-}
        EXPO_PUBLIC_HOME_STATE: ${WEB_HOME_STATE:-}
    depends_on:
      api: { condition: service_healthy }
    environment:
      # The push network's subnet, which the app's and the console's sites refuse (3f).
      PUSH_SUBNET: ${PUSH_SUBNET:-172.16.91.0/24}
      # The app's site, open (the default) or closed: closed answers 503 to every path while a restore is checked (3f,
      # section 7.17). Caddy reads it when it starts and refuses to start on any other value.
      APP_SITE: ${APP_SITE:-open}
    volumes:
      - caddy-data:/data
      - caddy-config:/config
    networks: [edge, app, push]

  cloudflared:
    image: cloudflare/cloudflared:2026.9.1@sha256:b269e8abd07a5bf6f3f4be65d5050b2174eca89c56a0241a8ff32a16aec454e4
    restart: unless-stopped
    read_only: true
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    logging: *logging
    profiles: ["tunnel"]
    command: ["tunnel", "--no-autoupdate", "run"]
    environment:
      TUNNEL_TOKEN: ${TUNNEL_TOKEN}
    networks: [edge]
    depends_on:
      - caddy

# cloudflared reaches only Caddy, Caddy reaches only the API and ntfy, and the API alone reaches the data services, but
# for the watcher's own network to PostgreSQL (3f).
networks:
  edge:
  app:
  data:
  # The watcher and PostgreSQL, nothing else. Not internal: the mail host's port 993 is reached through its gateway.
  watch:
  # ntfy, the watcher and Caddy. Internal: no route out. Its fixed subnet is what the app's and the console's sites refuse.
  push:
    internal: true
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: ${PUSH_SUBNET:-172.16.91.0/24}

volumes:
  # PostgreSQL 18. The earlier pgdata volume (PostgreSQL 16) stays until scripts/pg-major-upgrade.mjs has
  # moved it and you remove it by hand.
  pgdata18:
  valkeydata:
  # Uploads wait here for the worker and are deleted once processed. Nothing in it needs a backup.
  media-uploads:
  # The images korbat serves. Back it up together with the database.
  media-store:
  # 3d: the files of images sealed for good, moved out of the store by the quarantine service, on the host's encrypted
  # disk. It is in no backup, by decision: a restore never brings a destroyed file back. Owned by uid 1000, mode 0700, the
  # path the API's image makes (the README, Quarantine and Backups).
  media-quarantine:
  # Caddy's state, owned by its own user; the earlier root-owned caddydata and caddyconfig volumes can go.
  caddy-data:
  caddy-config:
  # ntfy's message cache and its auth database (3f). The cache is how a phone gets an alert published while its
  # connection was down; the auth database is rebuilt from infra/ntfy/server.yml at every start.
  ntfy-data:
```

```ts
/**
 * What a program may do (3d design, sections 2 rows 14 to 25, 6.6, 7.9 and 10.1; Task 6): the numbers of the automated
 * decision, mirrored from the database's automation_rules(), which a database test holds member for column; the closed
 * lists of a signal and of a cap's limit, each the CHECK of its column or the detail its refusal carries; and the sweep's
 * batch. It imports nothing, so every other module of the contracts can read it while it loads.
 */

/**
 * The mirror of automation_rules() (section 6.6's table). The caps are counted by rule: R1's decisions an hour and a day,
 * and R2's apart, so a burst of scores never uses up the seals of known matches (row 18). `unansweredMax` measures of a
 * program under one rule in force stop new ones under that rule, and a request for a person older than
 * `unansweredHours` stops new ones under either. `r1Threshold` is null until the owner's build task measures one (row
 * 23): while it is null no score opens anything. `objectionTargetHours` is the published target of an answer to "Ask for
 * a person" (row 25), never a time after which a measure ends. The rest are the numbers of known material (rows 33 to 37),
 * which its task reads.
 */
export const AUTOMATION_RULES: {
  readonly decisionsPerHour: number;
  readonly decisionsPerDay: number;
  readonly r2DecisionsPerHour: number;
  readonly r2DecisionsPerDay: number;
  readonly unansweredMax: number;
  readonly unansweredHours: number;
  readonly refusalsPerHour: number;
  readonly noReportHours: number;
  readonly r1Threshold: number | null;
  readonly r1ThresholdVersion: number;
  readonly objectionTargetHours: number;
  readonly matchTimeoutMs: number;
  readonly matchRetryHours: number;
  readonly matcherDownMinutes: number;
  readonly pdqMinQuality: number;
  readonly matchKeepDays: number;
} = {
  decisionsPerHour: 20,
  decisionsPerDay: 100,
  r2DecisionsPerHour: 20,
  r2DecisionsPerDay: 100,
  unansweredMax: 20,
  unansweredHours: 72,
  refusalsPerHour: 20,
  noReportHours: 24,
  r1Threshold: null,
  r1ThresholdVersion: 1,
  objectionTargetHours: 24,
  matchTimeoutMs: 3000,
  matchRetryHours: 24,
  matcherDownMinutes: 15,
  pdqMinQuality: 50,
  matchKeepDays: 180,
};

/**
 * The test scorer's own threshold and its version (section 5, "The threshold while only the test adapter exists"): under
 * R1_CLASSIFIER=test the API compares a score with 0.5 and records the threshold version 0, so the suite exercises the
 * whole path and no stored signal can be mistaken for one of a real model, whose versions start at 1.
 */
export const R1_TEST_THRESHOLD = { threshold: 0.5, thresholdVersion: 0 } as const;

/** The kinds of a signal (automated_signals.kind): a score at or over the threshold, or a match record (Task 7). */
export const SIGNAL_KINDS = ["r1_score", "known_match"] as const;
export type SignalKind = (typeof SIGNAL_KINDS)[number];

/**
 * What the step did with a signal (automated_signals.handled): a finding without a measure; a finding and its measure;
 * a finding whose measure a cap or a limit refused; a finding whose measure another measure already stood for; or
 * nothing, since the image, its post or its author left first.
 */
export const SIGNAL_HANDLED = ["finding", "measure", "capped", "covered", "gone"] as const;
export type SignalHandled = (typeof SIGNAL_HANDLED)[number];

/**
 * The limit a refusal automation_capped met, its detail and the fact of the alert automation_capped: the hour's or the
 * day's decisions of a program under one rule, its measures under one rule left unanswered, or a request for a person
 * that has waited too long.
 */
export const CAP_LIMITS = ["hour", "day", "unanswered", "waiting"] as const;
export type CapLimit = (typeof CAP_LIMITS)[number];

/** How many signals one round of the sweep takes at most, and how far back it looks (section 7.9). */
export const SWEEP_BATCH = 20;
export const SWEEP_HOURS = 24;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- known material (3d design, sections 2 rows 26 to 37, 6.7, 7.8 and 10.1; Task 7)

/** How many unanswered or capped checks one round of the job match-retry asks again at most (7.8 step 6). */
export const MATCH_RETRY_BATCH = 20;

/**
 * The state of an upload's comparison (media_hashes.check_state): waiting for its first answer; answered clear or
 * matched; unanswered in time, so the upload was accepted and the check is asked again for matchRetryHours; or an acting
 * match over the limit on refusals an hour, so the upload waits unposted, untold and unrefused until the check is asked
 * again.
 */
export const CHECK_STATES = ["pending", "clear", "matched", "unchecked", "capped"] as const;
export type MatchCheckState = (typeof CHECK_STATES)[number];

/** The hash a match rests on (media_matches.hash_type): three cryptographic hashes of the bytes as received, or PDQ. */
export const MATCH_HASH_TYPES = ["sha256", "sha1", "md5", "pdq"] as const;
export type MatchHashType = (typeof MATCH_HASH_TYPES)[number];

/** The kind of match as the source reports it (media_matches.match_kind). Only `exact` acts, and only of a listed class. */
export const MATCH_KINDS = ["exact", "near"] as const;
export type MatchKind = (typeof MATCH_KINDS)[number];

/** How an admin ends a held upload's hold (upload_refusals.end_as): neither is a default, and the console preselects neither. */
export const UPLOAD_ENDS = ["report", "no_report"] as const;
export type UploadEnd = (typeof UPLOAD_ENDS)[number];

/** The reason of an end as no_report (upload_refusals.end_reason), a closed list. */
export const UPLOAD_END_REASONS = ["source_withdrew", "counsel_no_duty", "other"] as const;
export type UploadEndReason = (typeof UPLOAD_END_REASONS)[number];

/** The console's words for each reason of an end as no_report (8.6), held to the list by a test. */
export const UPLOAD_END_REASON_LABELS: Record<UploadEndReason, string> = {
  source_withdrew: "The source withdrew or corrected its entry",
  counsel_no_duty: "Counsel: no duty to report this",
  other: "Another reason, written in the operator's notes",
};

/**
 * The reason of an admin's answer without a seal on a case whose match is acting (decisions.match_answer_reason, note
 * 26): it puts an image with an exact match back before everyone with nobody having looked.
 */
export const MATCH_ANSWER_REASONS = ["source_withdrew", "counsel", "other"] as const;
export type MatchAnswerReason = (typeof MATCH_ANSWER_REASONS)[number];

/** The console's words for each reason (8.4), held to the list by a test. */
export const MATCH_ANSWER_REASON_LABELS: Record<MatchAnswerReason, string> = {
  source_withdrew: "The source withdrew or corrected its entry",
  counsel: "Counsel's advice, written in the operator's notes",
  other: "Another reason, written in the operator's notes",
};

/**
 * The statement's `matchKind`, derived and never copied (W.3): `exact` only for an exact match of a cryptographic hash of
 * the file's bytes, `near` for every match of a perceptual hash whatever the source called it, since an equal perceptual
 * hash says that two pictures look alike, not that two files are the same.
 */
export function statementMatchKind(hashType: MatchHashType, matchKind: MatchKind): MatchKind {
  return hashType !== "pdq" && matchKind === "exact" ? "exact" : "near";
}
```

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { FORBIDDEN_FORMAT } from "./text";

/** Every code the media endpoints add to ErrorEnvelope.error.code (plus the shared ones: invalid_request, not_found, rate_limited). */
// 3d Task 7 (design, sections 7.8 step 5 and 10.7): upload_refused, a post that attaches an upload korbat did not accept.
export const MediaErrorCode = z.enum(["unsupported_media_type", "file_too_large", "too_many_pending_uploads", "uploads_unavailable", "media_unavailable", "upload_refused"]);
export type MediaErrorCode = z.infer<typeof MediaErrorCode>;

/** Why processing an upload failed. Reported on the status response, not as an HTTP error. */
export const MediaFailure = z.enum(["unsupported_format", "animated_not_supported", "image_too_large", "corrupt_image", "processing_failed"]);
export type MediaFailure = z.infer<typeof MediaFailure>;

/** 20 MiB. The API counts bytes while it streams an upload to disk and stops here. */
export const MEDIA_MAX_BYTES = 20 * 1024 * 1024;
export const MEDIA_MAX_PER_POST = 4;
/** The types an upload may declare. The bytes decide; the declaration is checked and then forgotten. */
export const MEDIA_ACCEPTED_TYPES = ["image/jpeg", "image/png", "image/webp", "image/avif", "image/gif"] as const;
export type MediaAcceptedType = (typeof MEDIA_ACCEPTED_TYPES)[number];
export const ALT_MAX_LENGTH = 1000;

/** A media id in its canonical lowercase form, which is also how it names files on the media volumes. */
export const MediaId = z.uuid().transform((id) => id.toLowerCase());

export const MEDIA_SIZES = ["small", "large"] as const;
export type MediaSize = (typeof MEDIA_SIZES)[number];

/** Where an image file is served. Views carry these paths, so the server can move images without a client change. */
export function mediaPath(id: string, size: MediaSize): string {
  return `/api/media/${id}/${size}.webp`;
}

/** Length in code points, which is what Postgres char_length counts. */
export function altLength(alt: string): number {
  return Array.from(alt).length;
}

/** Unicode NFC, every run of whitespace (line breaks included) to one space, trimmed. The server and the composer use the same rule. */
export function normalizeAltText(raw: string): string {
  return raw.normalize("NFC").replace(/\s+/gu, " ").trim();
}

const CONTROL = /\p{Cc}/u;

/** An image description as stored: normalized, 1 to 1000 code points, no control characters. */
export const AltText = z
  .string()
  .max(4000)
  .transform(normalizeAltText)
  .refine((alt) => !CONTROL.test(alt), { message: "control characters are not allowed" })
  .refine((alt) => !FORBIDDEN_FORMAT.test(alt), { message: "invisible direction and spacing characters are not allowed" })
  .refine((alt) => altLength(alt) >= 1, { message: "every image needs a description" })
  .refine((alt) => altLength(alt) <= ALT_MAX_LENGTH, { message: `descriptions have at most ${ALT_MAX_LENGTH} characters` });

/** One image of a new post: an upload that is ready, and its description. */
export const MediaAttachment = z.object({ id: MediaId, alt: AltText });
export type MediaAttachment = z.infer<typeof MediaAttachment>;

export const UploadResponse = z.object({ id: MediaId, status: z.literal("processing") });
export type UploadResponse = z.infer<typeof UploadResponse>;

/**
 * The state of one upload, for its owner. Width and height are those of the large size, after rotation. A ready image
 * carries its blurhash, except one that moderation sealed: it is shown to nobody, and the blurhash is made from the image.
 * 3d (design, sections 7.1, 9.6 and 10.2): a ready image on a post whose seal was lifted and whose files are not back in
 * the image store yet says `restoring`, and one whose files korbat recorded as lost says `lost`; at most one of the two.
 */
export const MediaStatusResponse = z
  .discriminatedUnion("status", [
    z.object({ id: MediaId, status: z.literal("processing") }),
    z.object({
      id: MediaId,
      status: z.literal("ready"),
      width: z.number().int().positive(),
      height: z.number().int().positive(),
      blurhash: z.string().min(6).optional(),
      restoring: z.literal(true).optional(),
      lost: z.literal(true).optional(),
    }),
    z.object({ id: MediaId, status: z.literal("failed"), error: MediaFailure }),
    // 3d Task 7 (design, sections 7.8 step 5 and 10.2): an upload korbat refused on an acting match, with the refusal's id
    // for the link to its notice and nothing of the file: no blurhash, no sizes. An upload whose check is capped answers
    // processing, as any upload that is still being processed.
    z.object({ id: MediaId, status: z.literal("refused"), refusalId: z.uuid() }),
  ])
  .refine((answer) => !(answer.status === "ready" && answer.restoring && answer.lost), { message: "an image is either being restored or lost, never both" });
export type MediaStatusResponse = z.infer<typeof MediaStatusResponse>;

/**
 * An image on a post, as a reader who is shown it gets it. `moderation` is set only on the author's own image that
 * moderation withheld or removed, with that state: the author keeps seeing such an image, and nobody else is shown it.
 */
export const MediaView = z.object({
  id: MediaId,
  width: z.number().int().positive(),
  height: z.number().int().positive(),
  blurhash: z.string().min(6),
  alt: z.string(),
  small: z.string(),
  large: z.string(),
  moderation: z.enum(["withheld", "removed"]).optional(),
});
export type MediaView = z.infer<typeof MediaView>;

/**
 * What a reader gets in place of an image they are not shown: its id and the mark, never its size, its blurhash, its
 * description or a path. It is what anyone but the author gets for a withheld or removed image, the same for both states,
 * and what everyone gets for a sealed image, its author included: `sealed` is set only then, and only for the author.
 */
export const HiddenMedia = z.strictObject({ id: MediaId, hidden: z.literal(true), sealed: z.literal(true).optional() });
export type HiddenMedia = z.infer<typeof HiddenMedia>;

/** Whether an entry of a post's media list is a hidden image, which has nothing to draw or to open. */
export function isHiddenMedia(item: MediaView | HiddenMedia): item is HiddenMedia {
  return "hidden" in item;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the edge (3d design, sections 2 rows 11 to 13, 7.4 and 10.1)

/**
 * The two numbers of a public image's Cache-Control header (3d Task 3), which the API builds the header from: a browser
 * keeps a copy at most `browserSeconds`, an edge at most `edgeSeconds`, and neither serves a stale one. They are the
 * bound korbat states for a hidden image's copy without an accepted purge, and every sentence that states it prints them
 * from here.
 */
export const EDGE_CACHE = {
  browserSeconds: 60,
  edgeSeconds: 300,
} as const;

/**
 * The outbox's job (7.4): at most `prefixes` images a request and one request a round, a round `roundSeconds` after the
 * last ended (so at most four a minute), each request bounded at `timeoutMs`; a failed row waits `backoffSeconds`, doubled
 * at each failure up to `backoffMaxSeconds`, and is given up `giveUpHours` after it was written; the retention job (Task 8)
 * deletes a row `keepDays` after it was done.
 */
export const EDGE_RULES = {
  prefixes: 30,
  roundSeconds: 15,
  timeoutMs: 5000,
  backoffSeconds: 30,
  backoffMaxSeconds: 3600,
  giveUpHours: 24,
  keepDays: 30,
} as const;

/** The numbers the words about the edge print, in the units they print them: the edge's bound in minutes and the hours of the give-up. */
export const EDGE_WORDS = {
  edgeMinutes: EDGE_CACHE.edgeSeconds / 60,
  giveUpHours: EDGE_RULES.giveUpHours,
} as const;

/** Why an image stopped being public: a state, the image's or its post's; a deletion or an erasure; a release (the CHECK of edge_purges.cause). */
export const EDGE_PURGE_CAUSES = ["state", "deleted", "released"] as const;
export type EdgePurgeCause = (typeof EDGE_PURGE_CAUSES)[number];

/** How an outbox row ended: the provider took the purge, it gave up, or no adapter was on (the CHECK of edge_purges.outcome). */
export const EDGE_PURGE_OUTCOMES = ["accepted", "failed", "off"] as const;
export type EdgePurgeOutcome = (typeof EDGE_PURGE_OUTCOMES)[number];

/**
 * One image's newest outbox row as staff read it (10.3), on a case and on an order's item: its outcome, or `pending` while
 * it has none, and its time (when it ended, or when it was written while it is pending). An image that never stopped
 * being public has no row and no entry.
 */
export const EdgePurgeView = z.strictObject({
  mediaId: z.uuid(),
  outcome: z.enum([...EDGE_PURGE_OUTCOMES, "pending"]),
  at: z.iso.datetime(),
});
export type EdgePurgeView = z.infer<typeof EdgePurgeView>;
```

```ts
// the mails and the terms share. Each is the one source its words and numbers are taken from. This module imports

// shapes may come to name this module's constants: what a notice needs of a post's id and of a handle is written here.

 * The migration's CHECK lists are written from this constant, and a database test holds them to it. A value the
 * Commission removes stays here: a kept row may hold it, and only the lists offered for new input drop it.
 */

  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CONSUMER_INFORMATION",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE_AGAINST_WOMEN",

  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH",

  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC",

  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_UNSAFE_AND_PROHIBITED_PRODUCTS",

] as const;

export type TdbFormCategory = Exclude<TdbCategory, UnofferedCategory>;

/** The 14 categories the illegal-ground form shows. */
export const TDB_FORM_CATEGORIES: readonly TdbFormCategory[] = TDB_CATEGORIES.filter(
  (category): category is TdbFormCategory => category !== "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC" && category !== "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE",
);

/**
 * The four choices of the path for child sexual abuse material and the Transparency Database keyword each stores. "abuse"
 * stores none: the database has no keyword for it.
 */
export const CSAM_KEYWORDS = {
  csam: "KEYWORD_CHILD_SEXUAL_ABUSE_MATERIAL",
  deepfake: "KEYWORD_CHILD_SEXUAL_ABUSE_MATERIAL_DEEPFAKE",
  grooming: "KEYWORD_GROOMING_SEXUAL_ENTICEMENT_MINORS",
  abuse: null,
} as const;
export type CsamKeywordChoice = keyof typeof CSAM_KEYWORDS;

/** The keywords a decision on the law may carry: in 3c only the Transparency Database's "Terrorist content". */
export const DECISION_KEYWORDS = ["KEYWORD_TERRORIST_CONTENT"] as const;
export type DecisionKeyword = (typeof DECISION_KEYWORDS)[number];

/** The category the composer presets for a decision under each rule. */
export const RULE_DEFAULT_CATEGORY = {
  R1: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC",
  R2: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS",
  R3: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH",
  R4: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS",
  R5: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE",
  R6: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SCAMS_AND_FRAUD",
} as const satisfies Record<RuleId, TdbCategory>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- lanes

/** The queue's lanes: 0 is the most urgent. A case takes the most severe lane of its unanswered items. */
export type Lane = 0 | 1 | 2;

/** R2 and R5 are urgent; R3 and R4 come next; R1 and R6 last. */
const RULE_LANES: Record<RuleId, Lane> = { R1: 2, R2: 0, R3: 1, R4: 1, R5: 0, R6: 2 };

/** The categories that are not in lane 2: violence, public security and self-harm are urgent; six more come next. */
const CATEGORY_LANES: Partial<Record<TdbCategory, Lane>> = {
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE: 0,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_RISK_FOR_PUBLIC_SECURITY: 0,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SELF_HARM: 0,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS: 1,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE: 1,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE_AGAINST_WOMEN: 1,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH: 1,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS: 1,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE: 1,
};

/**
 * The lane of an intake's items, from its ground alone: nothing is weighted. The CSAM path is urgent whatever else is
 * said. Otherwise it is the more severe of the cited rule's lane and, on a notice that alleges illegality, the category's:
 * only there is the category a claim about the content, where on a rule report or a finding it is korbat's own
 * classification for the Transparency Database.
 */
export function laneFor(input: { ruleId: RuleId | null; allegesIllegal: boolean; csam: boolean; category: TdbCategory }): Lane {
  if (input.csam) return 0;
  const byRule: Lane = input.ruleId === null ? 2 : RULE_LANES[input.ruleId];
  const byCategory: Lane = input.allegesIllegal ? (CATEGORY_LANES[input.category] ?? 2) : 2;
  return byRule < byCategory ? byRule : byCategory;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- limits and periods

/**
 * What one sender may send, published in the terms: intakes an hour and a day per network signed out and per account
 * signed in, the targets one notice names, and the bounds of its two texts in characters (the migration's CHECKs hold
 * the same numbers).
 */
export const NOTICE_LIMITS = {
  signedOut: { perHour: 5, perDay: 20 },
  signedIn: { perHour: 10, perDay: 50 },
  maxTargets: 10,
  explanationMax: 2000,
  citedLawMax: 300,
} as const;

/** A notice on the CSAM path names at most one account: one such target reaches every image on the account's posts. */
export const CSAM_NOTICE_MAX_ACCOUNTS = 1;

/** How many months back a case page counts earlier answers to reports of this kind about the same target or author. */
export const SUSPECT_EARLIER_MONTHS = 12;

/** How many rows of a seal's list the case answer carries. */
export const SEAL_LIST_MAX = 500;

/** The author's appeal and the re-examination window, in calendar months (appealDeadline, and appeal_deadline in SQL). */
export const APPEAL_MONTHS = 6;

/** Appeals a day per account, and re-examinations a day per account or network. */
export const DAILY_LIMITS = { appeals: 5, reexaminations: 5 } as const;

/**
 * The numbers of account sanctions, the same as the SQL function standing_rules() returns, which a database test compares
 * member by member: every function and view of the standing ledger reads its numbers from there, and every word of the
 * console and the app from here. Each is a cautious default without a source of its own, flagged for the owner (3e
 * design, section 2): one line to change in each place. It stands here, ahead of the section of account sanctions below,
 * because RETENTION reads three of its numbers.
 */
export const STANDING_RULES = {
  /** How long a strike counts. */

  /** The active strikes that open the ladder. */
  ladderStrikes: 3,
  /** The most days of the first, second and third suspension of the ladder. */
  ladderDays: [3, 7, 30],
  /** How long a suspension of the ladder counts toward the next rung. */
  ladderMemoryDays: 365,
  /** The reply window, from the moment korbat's own relay accepted the notice mail, and never less from the decision. */
  replyWindowHours: 168,
  /** The window, from the decision, when the relay refused the address or the mail was given up. */
  undeliveredHours: 336,
  /** The most days of a suspension at once, by its ground. */
  threatDays: 30,
  terroristDays: 30,
  floodDays: 7,
  protectiveDays: 14,
  /** The count without which no flood is found: a condition, never the finding. */
  floodPosts: 20,
  floodMinutes: 60,
  /** The most age of the decision a threat or terrorist suspension rests on, and of the seal for good a protective one rests on. */
  basisAgeDays: 30,
  /** The frame of the reporting counts, by the day a report was sent, and a warning's time of counting. */
  reportFrameDays: 90,
  /** The warning's threshold: marked reports, and their share of the rule reports sent. */
  reportWarnMarks: 5,
  reportWarnShare: 0.5,
  /** The restriction's threshold, in marked reports sent after the warning, and its most days. */
  reportRestrictMarks: 3,
  reportRestrictDays: 30,
} as const;

/**
 * How long 3c keeps each kind of data (the design's section 6.6), published in the terms. Each is a design choice, not a
 * legal figure.
 */
export const RETENTION = {
  /** Content restricted under R4 is erased once the restriction is final: this long after its author was told, or at the answer to their appeal. */
  r4FinalMonths: APPEAL_MONTHS,
  /** An intake's record (its texts and who sent it) goes this long after its last release. */
  intakeDays: 30,
  /** A reset field's old value stays readable this long after a lift that comes before the case's copies are erased. */
  resetValueDays: 30,
  /** A case's evidence waits this long after the case's newest snapshot or draft text. */
  evidenceHours: 24,
  /** Statements are erased this long after the account's deletion. */
  statementMonths: 12,
  /** The access log, and the reveal reasons its rows name. */
  accessLogMonths: 12,
  /** A notifier's contact goes this long after the last day korbat owed the notice something, */
  contactMonths: 6,
  /** and at most this long after the notice when nothing moved that day. */
  contactMaxMonths: 13,
  /** A notifier's confirmation of an address. */
  confirmationDays: 30,
  /** Backups are deleted this long after each was taken. No code of 3c enforces it: the README tells the operator. */
  backupDays: 30,
  /** An unconfirmed staff text is deleted after this long. */
  draftHours: 24,
  /** A mail still unsent this long after it was due is given up. */
  mailGiveUpDays: 5,
  /**
   * 3e (design, sections 6.5, 6.7 and W.7): the text of a reply to a suspension or a termination is kept until it is
   * answered and its decision is final for its author (erase_reply_statements); an unanswered reply keeps it, however
   * old. No clock alone ends it, so it is a phrase, the one the terms print, and no number.
   */
  replyText: "until korbat has answered it and its decision can no longer be appealed",
  /**
   * 3e: the reporting counts (the marks "manifestly unfounded" and the daily tallies of rule reports) are deleted this
   * long after the UTC day their report was sent (forget_report_counts), and with the account. It is the frame of the
   * counts, read from STANDING_RULES and never typed twice.
   */
  reportCountDays: STANDING_RULES.reportFrameDays,
  /**
   * 3e: the ledger rows of strikes, suspensions, terminations, warnings and retired handles are kept with their decision,
   * as every row of the ledger is; what ends is their use, after these days: a strike's counting, a suspension's memory
   * toward the next rung, and a warning's counting. Each is STANDING_RULES' own number.
   */
  standingRecord: { strikeDays: STANDING_RULES.strikeDays, ladderMemoryDays: STANDING_RULES.ladderMemoryDays, warningDays: STANDING_RULES.reportFrameDays },
  /**
   * 3f (design, sections 6.8 and 10.1, W.6): how long a handled message at the contact point is kept (one never handled
   * is kept until a person closes it), how long what a removal order disabled is preserved from its disabling (and a day
   * more, ORDER_RULES.preserveMarginDays), how long an order's records and those of a notification or a production are
   * kept after the matter's last event, and a restore gap closed as not needed or imported. Each is order_rules()' own
   * number, read from ORDER_RULES and printed by the terms; the database holds the same numbers and acts on them.
   */
  contactMessageDays: ORDER_RULES.messageKeepDays,
  orderPreserveMonths: ORDER_RULES.preserveMonths,
  orderRecordYears: ORDER_RULES.recordKeepYears,
  restoreGapMonths: ORDER_RULES.gapKeepMonths,
} as const;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- account sanctions (3e design, section 10.1)

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- measures

/**
 * The ledger's kinds, in the order of the database's action_kind: 3c's seven measures and five reversals, then 3e's six
 * measures (a strike, a suspension, a termination, a retired handle, a warning about reporting and a restriction of it)
 * and four reversals (3e design, section 10.1); then 3f's measure of an authority's order and its reversal (3f design,
 * section 10.1), which only an order decision and its correction hold.
 */
export const ACTION_KINDS = [
  "withhold",
  "remove",
  "seal_media",
  "withhold_media",
  "remove_media",
  "reset_display_name",
  "reset_bio",
  "restore",
  "unseal_media",
  "restore_media",
  "restore_display_name",
  "restore_bio",
  "strike",
  "suspend",
  "terminate",
  "retire_handle",
  "warn_reporting",
  "restrict_reporting",
  "overrule",
  "lift_suspension",
  "unretire_handle",
  "lift_reporting",
  "disable_by_order",
  "reinstate_by_order",
] as const;
export type ActionKind = (typeof ACTION_KINDS)[number];

/**
 * What a measure acts on: a post, one image of it, every image its case reaches, one of an account's two fields, the
 * account itself (a strike, a suspension or a termination), its handle, or its reports under the rules.
 */
export type MeasureTarget = "post" | "image" | "images" | "display_name" | "bio" | "account" | "handle" | "reporting";

export interface MeasureSpec {
  /** A decision taken while deciding (interim) may hold it. */
  interim: boolean;
  /** A decision that decides the case (final) may hold it. */
  final: boolean;
  /** For a reversal, the measures it lifts (it names exactly one row of them); null for a measure. */
  lifts: readonly ActionKind[] | null;
  target: MeasureTarget;
  /** The words for it in the composer, the statement and the terms. */
  label: string;
}

/**
 * Every kind of the ledger: whether it is taken while deciding, when the case is decided, or is a reversal; its target;
 * and its label. A post or one image is withheld only while deciding and removed only when the case is decided; a seal
 * and a field reset are either. A reversal is neither: the database's triggers say which decision may hold one.
 */
export const MEASURES = {
  withhold: { interim: true, final: false, lifts: null, target: "post", label: "Withhold the post" },
  remove: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "post", label: "Remove" },
  seal_media: { interim: true, final: true, lifts: null, target: "images", label: "Seal the images this case reaches" },
  withhold_media: { interim: true, final: false, lifts: null, target: "image", label: "Withhold one image" },
  remove_media: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "image", label: "Remove one image" },
  reset_display_name: { interim: true, final: true, lifts: null, target: "display_name", label: "Reset display name" },
  reset_bio: { interim: true, final: true, lifts: null, target: "bio", label: "Reset bio" },
  restore: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["withhold", "remove"], target: "post", label: "Lift the restriction of the post" },
  unseal_media: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["seal_media"], target: "images", label: "Lift the seal" },
  restore_media: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["withhold_media", "remove_media"], target: "image", label: "Lift the restriction of one image" },
  restore_display_name: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["reset_display_name"], target: "display_name", label: "Lift the reset of the display name" },
  restore_bio: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["reset_bio"], target: "bio", label: "Lift the reset of the bio" },
  // 3e (design, section 18, W.1). Each measure of 3e is taken only when the case is decided, and none while deciding.
  strike: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "account", label: "Strike" },
  suspend: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "account", label: "Suspend the account" },
  terminate: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "account", label: "Terminate the account" },
  retire_handle: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "handle", label: "Retire the handle" },
  warn_reporting: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "reporting", label: "Warn about reporting" },
  restrict_reporting: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "reporting", label: "Restrict reporting" },
  overrule: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["strike"], target: "account", label: "Overrule the strike" },
  lift_suspension: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["suspend", "terminate"], target: "account", label: "Lift the suspension" },
  unretire_handle: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["retire_handle"], target: "handle", label: "Give the handle back" },
  lift_reporting: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["warn_reporting", "restrict_reporting"], target: "reporting", label: "Lift the reporting measure" },
  // 3f (design, section 18, W.1): neither is taken while deciding or when a case is decided; only an order decision holds
  // the first, and only the correction of one the second.
  disable_by_order: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: null, target: "post", label: "Disabled for an order" },
  reinstate_by_order: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["disable_by_order"], target: "post", label: "Reinstate after an order" },
} as const satisfies Record<ActionKind, MeasureSpec>;

/** The fourteen measures and the ten reversals, each list in the ledger's order: what a statement's data keeps apart. */
export const MEASURE_KINDS = [
  "withhold",
  "remove",
  "seal_media",
  "withhold_media",
  "remove_media",
  "reset_display_name",
  "reset_bio",
  "strike",
  "suspend",
  "terminate",
  "retire_handle",
  "warn_reporting",
  "restrict_reporting",
  "disable_by_order",
] as const satisfies readonly ActionKind[];
export type MeasureKind = (typeof MEASURE_KINDS)[number];
export const REVERSAL_KINDS = ["restore", "unseal_media", "restore_media", "restore_display_name", "restore_bio", "overrule", "lift_suspension", "unretire_handle", "lift_reporting", "reinstate_by_order"] as const satisfies readonly ActionKind[];
export type ReversalKind = (typeof REVERSAL_KINDS)[number];

/** The three kinds whose action entry also signs `days` and `announced` (3e design, section 10.4). */
export const TIMED_KINDS = ["suspend", "terminate", "restrict_reporting"] as const satisfies readonly ActionKind[];
export type TimedKind = (typeof TIMED_KINDS)[number];

/**
 * The console's fixed drafts of the facts and the reason of a seal (3c design, section 10). Nobody at korbat opens images
 * that are reported as child sexual abuse material, so none of these says or implies that korbat found them to be such
 * material, and each reason says that korbat's staff do not open them: the statement then tells its author what korbat
 * knows and no more. The composer fills them in, and the moderator may edit them. The two `added` drafts are for a case
 * whose suspect items korbat added for a quoted post: they never say that this post was reported, and name no other post.
 */
export const SEAL_DRAFTS = {
  facts: {
    notice_post: "korbat received a notice that reports images of this post as child sexual abuse material.",
    notice_account: "korbat received a notice that reports this account for child sexual abuse material. It does not say which images, so korbat sealed every image on the account's posts.",
    notice_added: "korbat received a notice about content on korbat that shows this post's images and reports them as child sexual abuse material.",
    finding_post: "A moderator reported images of this post as possible child sexual abuse material.",
    finding_account: "A moderator reported images on this account's posts as possible child sexual abuse material. korbat sealed every image on the account's posts.",
    finding_added: "A moderator reported content on korbat that shows this post's images as possible child sexual abuse material.",
    /**
     * 3d Task 7 (W.3): a seal for good on a case whose only suspect items are a program's. {comparison} is W.3's clause of
     * the comparison (@korbat/rules), with "this post" for "your post" and a capital letter, which the console fills in;
     * the draft says what the comparison found and not that anyone reported the images, and holds no hash, no list version
     * and no classification string.
     */
    match_post: "{comparison}. korbat's staff do not open such an image, and korbat has not assessed it.",
  },
  reason: {
```
