```ts
/**
 * The watcher's one row: its heartbeat after each round, when it last read both folders and last published (or owed
 * nothing), and the word of its last failure. The API reads it for the channel's health.
 */
export const notifyState = pgTable(
  "notify_state",
  {
    id: smallint("id").primaryKey(),
    beatAt: ts("beat_at"),
    mailboxOkAt: ts("mailbox_ok_at"),
    pushOkAt: ts("push_ok_at"),
    /** Null, or one of the contracts' NOTIFY_ERRORS. */
    error: text("error"),
  },
  (t) => [
    check("notify_state_single_row", sql`${t.id} = 1`),
    check("notify_state_error", sql`${t.error} in ('imap_connect', 'imap_timeout', 'imap_tls', 'imap_login', 'imap_folder', 'imap_protocol', 'push_connect', 'push_refused')`),
    fullAccess("notify_state_api_all", apiRole),
    fullAccess("notify_state_notify_all", notifyRole),
  ],
).enableRLS();

/** The watcher's mark in each folder: the folder's UIDVALIDITY and the highest UID it has inserted. */
export const notifyFolders = pgTable(
  "notify_folders",
  {
    folder: text("folder").primaryKey(),
    uidvalidity: bigint("uidvalidity", { mode: "number" }),
    lastUid: bigint("last_uid", { mode: "number" }),
  },
  (t) => [check("notify_folders_folder", sql`${t.folder} in ('inbox', 'junk')`), fullAccess("notify_folders_api_all", apiRole), fullAccess("notify_folders_notify_all", notifyRole)],
).enableRLS();

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- records to authorities (3f design, section 6.5)
// The lists are written from the contracts' constants of the same meaning (NOTIFICATION_STATES, NOTIFICATION_DUTIES,
// NOTIFICATION_SENT_KINDS, NOTIFICATION_ANSWERS, NOTIFICATION_EVENT_KINDS, NOTIFICATION_OPENED_VIA,
// PRODUCTION_INSTRUMENTS, ACCESS_PURPOSES, PRODUCED_KINDS, NOT_HELD_KINDS): @korbat/db does not depend on
// @korbat/contracts, so a database test holds each migrated CHECK to its constant.
const NOTIFICATION_DUTIES = ["dsa18_1", "dsa18_2", "tco14_5", "voluntary"];
const NOTIFICATION_SENT_KINDS = ["handle", "address", "created_at", "post_ids", "post_times", "report_time", "files"];
const PRODUCED_KINDS = [...NOTIFICATION_SENT_KINDS, "content"];
const NOT_HELD_KINDS = ["name", "postal_address", "date_of_birth", "phone_number", "ip_address"];
/** The values as a SQL array of string literals: plain lower-case words of this file. */
const arrayOf = (values: readonly string[]) => sql.raw(`array[${values.map((value) => `'${value}'`).join(", ")}]::text[]`);

/**
 * One notification to an authority that is owed, sent or declined (3f design, sections 6.5 and 7.13). Only the command
 * line, as the migrator, reads and writes it, and the trigger report_open() opens one when a seal is taken: the API role
 * holds no grant, and its one policy lets it see no row. No column holds an address, a handle or a value that was sent; an
 * account, a case and a seal are named by their ids, without foreign keys, since the record outlives a purge and a case.
 * opened_at is forced, except that a row with imported_at keeps a supplied time that is not after the clock.
 */
export const authorityNotifications = pgTable(
  "authority_notifications",
  {
    id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
    state: text("state").notNull(),
    /** The duties it meets; empty while a seal's record is only owed. */
    duties: text("duties").array().notNull().default(sql`'{}'::text[]`),
    caseId: uuid("case_id"),
    /** The seal_media row that opened it; null for one the command line opened. */

    accountId: uuid("account_id"),
    openedAt: ts("opened_at").notNull(),
    openedVia: text("opened_via").notNull(),
    /** Awareness: the first suspect report's time, and the admin's answer's. */
    firstReportAt: ts("first_report_at"),
    adminAnswerAt: ts("admin_answer_at"),
    /** The check: who, when, yes or no, why. */
    checkedBy: text("checked_by"),
    checkedAt: ts("checked_at"),
    checkResult: boolean("check_result"),
    checkReason: text("check_reason"),
    /** An ISO code and why that state; or null and why none is identifiable. */
    stateConcerned: text("state_concerned"),
    stateBasis: text("state_basis"),
    authority: text("authority"),
    channel: text("channel"),
    sentAt: ts("sent_at"),
    receipt: text("receipt"),
    sentBy: text("sent_by"),
    ownReference: text("own_reference"),
    theirReference: text("their_reference"),
    /** What was sent, by kind, never by value. */
    sentKinds: text("sent_kinds").array(),
    /** Which version of the fixed sentence of what korbat does not hold went with it (RECORDS_NOT_HELD). */
    notKeptVersion: smallint("not_kept_version"),
    /** The authority's answer as one word, and its day. */
    answer: text("answer"),
    answeredAt: ts("answered_at"),
    /** `unsealed` when the database closed it; else the operator's reason. */
    declinedReason: text("declined_reason"),
    closedAt: ts("closed_at"),
    importedAt: ts("imported_at"),
  },
  (t) => [
    check("authority_notifications_state", sql`${t.state} in ('owed', 'sent', 'declined')`),
    check("authority_notifications_duties", sql`${t.duties} <@ ${arrayOf(NOTIFICATION_DUTIES)}`),
    check("authority_notifications_sent_kinds", sql`${t.sentKinds} <@ ${arrayOf(NOTIFICATION_SENT_KINDS)}`),
    check("authority_notifications_answer", sql`${t.answer} in ('not_illegal', 'illegal', 'no_assessment', 'other')`),
    check("authority_notifications_opened_via", sql`${t.openedVia} in ('system', 'cli')`),
    // A seal opens a record and names its row; the command line opens one for a duty and names no seal.
    check("authority_notifications_seal", sql`(${t.openedVia} = 'system') = (${t.sealActionId} is not null)`),
    check("authority_notifications_closed", sql`(${t.state} = 'owed') = (${t.closedAt} is null)`),
    check("authority_notifications_declined", sql`(${t.state} = 'declined') = (${t.declinedReason} is not null)`),
    check(
      "authority_notifications_sent",
      sql`${t.state} <> 'sent' or (${t.sentAt} is not null and ${t.authority} is not null and ${t.channel} is not null and ${t.sentKinds} is not null and cardinality(${t.duties}) > 0 and ${t.notKeptVersion} is not null)`,
    ),
    check("authority_notifications_answered", sql`${t.answer} is null or ${t.answeredAt} is not null`),
    check(
      "authority_notifications_texts",
      sql`char_length(${t.checkReason}) <= 500 and char_length(${t.stateBasis}) <= 500 and char_length(${t.declinedReason}) <= 500 and char_length(${t.checkedBy}) <= 200 and char_length(${t.sentBy}) <= 200 and char_length(${t.authority}) <= 200 and char_length(${t.channel}) <= 200 and char_length(${t.receipt}) <= 500 and char_length(${t.ownReference}) <= 200 and char_length(${t.theirReference}) <= 200`,
    ),
    /** One owed record a seal opened, for each account: a second seal finds it, and the trigger's lock orders the two. */
    uniqueIndex("authority_notifications_owed_seal_key").on(t.accountId).where(sql`state = 'owed' and opened_via = 'system'`),
    /** reports_owed() and the alert's count. */
    index("authority_notifications_owed_idx").on(t.openedAt).where(sql`state = 'owed'`),
    index("authority_notifications_account_idx").on(t.accountId),
    index("authority_notifications_case_idx").on(t.caseId),
    pgPolicy("authority_notifications_api_none", { for: "select", to: apiRole, using: sql`false` }),
  ],
).enableRLS();

/**
 * A later request or answer of the authority about a notification's matter, or the operator's note (7.13 step 6), with
 * the authority's demand that the person is not told and that demand's end, which may be open (null with the mark set).
 * `at` is forced, except for an imported record's event, which keeps a supplied time that is not after the clock.
 */
export const authorityNotificationEvents = pgTable(
  "authority_notification_events",
  {
    id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
    notificationId: uuid("notification_id")
      .notNull()
      .references(() => authorityNotifications.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
    kind: text("kind").notNull(),
    at: ts("at").notNull(),
    /** When the request or answer was made, as the authority dated it. */
    occurredAt: ts("occurred_at"),
    reference: text("reference"),
    /** How it came and what it asked, about the act and never about the person (at most 500 characters). */
    how: text("how").notNull(),
    notToPerson: boolean("not_to_person").notNull(),
    notToPersonUntil: ts("not_to_person_until"),
  },
  (t) => [
    check("authority_notification_events_kind", sql`${t.kind} in ('request', 'answer', 'note')`),
    check("authority_notification_events_until", sql`${t.notToPerson} or ${t.notToPersonUntil} is null`),
    check("authority_notification_events_texts", sql`char_length(${t.how}) between 1 and 500 and char_length(${t.reference}) <= 200`),
    index("authority_notification_events_notification_idx").on(t.notificationId, t.at),
    pgPolicy("authority_notification_events_api_none", { for: "select", to: apiRole, using: sql`false` }),
  ],
).enableRLS();

/**
 * One row for every time something leaves korbat for an authority (3f design, sections 6.5 and 7.14): account data for
 * an order or a notification, a hand-over of one seal's files, a seizure, an access to preserved content for an
 * authority. What was asked for, produced and not held is stored by kind, never as a text; a hand-over's files by name,
 * size and SHA-256. opened_at is forced as a notification's.
 */
export const productions = pgTable(
  "productions",
  {
    id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
    instrument: text("instrument").notNull(),
    notificationId: uuid("notification_id"),
    orderId: uuid("order_id"),
    orderItemId: uuid("order_item_id"),
    sealActionId: uuid("seal_action_id"),
    accountId: uuid("account_id"),
    /** For preserved_access alone: why the content was opened. */
    purpose: text("purpose"),
    authority: text("authority"),
    ownReference: text("own_reference"),
    theirReference: text("their_reference"),
    asked: text("asked").array(),
    produced: text("produced").array().notNull(),
    notHeld: text("not_held").array(),
    /** A hand-over: each listed file's name, and once recorded its size and SHA-256. */
    files: jsonb("files").$type<{ name: string; bytes: number | null; sha256: string | null }[]>(),
    archiveSha256: text("archive_sha256"),
    channel: text("channel"),
    receipt: text("receipt"),
    deliveredAt: ts("delivered_at"),
    destroyedAt: ts("destroyed_at"),
    destroyedHow: text("destroyed_how"),
    notToPersonUntil: ts("not_to_person_until"),
    openedAt: ts("opened_at").notNull(),
    recordedBy: text("recorded_by"),
    importedAt: ts("imported_at"),
  },
  (t) => [
    check("productions_instrument", sql`${t.instrument} in ('notification', 'demand', 'court_order', 'seizure', 'dsa_art10', 'preserved_access')`),
    check("productions_purpose", sql`(${t.instrument} = 'preserved_access') = (${t.purpose} is not null)`),
    // Compared as text: 'authority' is also a value 3f added to an enum (intake_channel), and the enum-literal rule reads
    // the migrations' words, not their types.
    check("productions_purposes", sql`${t.purpose}::text in ('review', 'complaint', 'authority')`),
    check("productions_asked", sql`${t.asked} <@ ${arrayOf(NOTIFICATION_SENT_KINDS)}`),
    check("productions_produced", sql`${t.produced} <@ ${arrayOf(PRODUCED_KINDS)}`),
    check("productions_not_held", sql`${t.notHeld} <@ ${arrayOf(NOT_HELD_KINDS)}`),
    check("productions_archive", sql`${t.archiveSha256} ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'`),
    check("productions_files", sql`jsonb_typeof(${t.files}) = 'array'`),
    check("productions_destroyed", sql`(${t.destroyedAt} is null) = (${t.destroyedHow} is null)`),
    check(
      "productions_texts",
      sql`char_length(${t.authority}) <= 200 and char_length(${t.ownReference}) <= 200 and char_length(${t.theirReference}) <= 200 and char_length(${t.channel}) <= 200 and char_length(${t.receipt}) <= 500 and char_length(${t.destroyedHow}) <= 500 and char_length(${t.recordedBy}) <= 200`,
    ),
    /** handover_undestroyed's count, and the records command's list. */
    index("productions_undestroyed_idx").on(t.deliveredAt).where(sql`files is not null and destroyed_at is null`),
    index("productions_account_idx").on(t.accountId),
    pgPolicy("productions_api_none", { for: "select", to: apiRole, using: sql`false` }),
  ],
).enableRLS();

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- recovery (3f design, section 6.6)
// The lists are the contracts' GAP_CLASSES and GAP_DISPOSITIONS, in the order the console and the import list them; a
// database test holds each migrated CHECK to its constant, as for the records above.
const GAP_CLASSES = ["order_effect", "seal_final", "seal_interim", "release", "standing", "restriction", "reversal", "no_measure", "record"];
const GAP_DISPOSITIONS = ["reapplied", "not_needed", "imported"];
const listOf = (values: readonly string[]) => sql.raw(values.map((value) => `'${value}'`).join(", "));

/**
 * One row for each lost decision and each lost record that an import after a restore found in the keeper's files (3f
 * design, sections 6.6 and 7.17): the lost audit row's place, hash, action, target, metadata and time, the class that
 * orders its taking again, and its closing. The API role reads it; the import writes it as the migrator, gap_close as its
 * owner, and a record command given --gap closes a gap of the class record. A gap names its closing decision by id
 * without a foreign key: the decision's statement reads the lost day from the gap for as long as the ledger keeps the
 * decision, and the fixtures that remove decisions must not be held by it.
 */
export const restoreGaps = pgTable(
  "restore_gaps",
  {
    id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
    /** One value for every gap one import wrote. */
    importId: uuid("import_id").notNull(),
    place: bigint("place", { mode: "number" }).notNull(),
    hash: text("hash").notNull(),
    action: text("action").notNull(),
    targetType: text("target_type"),
    /** An order_effected row gives one gap an item, with the item as its target. */
    targetId: text("target_id"),
    metadata: jsonb("metadata"),
    actedAt: ts("acted_at").notNull(),
    /** When the import that found it ran: the console's "After a restore" names the newest import's time. */
    importedAt: ts("imported_at").notNull(),
    class: text("class").notNull(),
    closedAt: ts("closed_at"),
    /** The decision that took the measure again; null for the dispositions not_needed and imported. */
    closedBy: uuid("closed_by"),
    disposition: text("disposition"),
  },
  (t) => [
    check("restore_gaps_class", sql`${t.class} in (${listOf(GAP_CLASSES)})`),
    check("restore_gaps_disposition", sql`${t.disposition} in (${listOf(GAP_DISPOSITIONS)})`),
    // Open, or closed with a disposition; a decision names the closing exactly when it took the measure again.
    check("restore_gaps_closed", sql`(${t.closedAt} is null) = (${t.disposition} is null) and (${t.closedBy} is not null) = (${t.disposition} is not distinct from 'reapplied')`),
    check("restore_gaps_hash", sql`${t.hash} ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'`),
    check("restore_gaps_place", sql`${t.place} > 0`),
    unique("restore_gaps_place_key").on(t.importId, t.place, t.targetId),
    /** The open gaps by class: the console's list, the home line and whether the app's site may open. */
    index("restore_gaps_open_idx").on(t.class).where(sql`closed_at is null`),
    fullAccess("restore_gaps_api_all", apiRole),
  ],
).enableRLS();

/**
 * The keeper's confirmations of the audit log's daily copy (3f design, sections 6.6 and 7.16): who holds the copy up to
 * which place, and when the database recorded it (forced clock_timestamp()). The mark route inserts one for a staff
 * member once the console holds the whole file; `staff.js audit-export` one under the system actor.
 */
export const copyMarks = pgTable(
  "copy_marks",
  {
    id: bigint("id", { mode: "number" }).primaryKey().generatedAlwaysAsIdentity(),
    staffId: uuid("staff_id").notNull(),
    /** The newest place the download held. */
    place: bigint("place", { mode: "number" }).notNull(),
    at: ts("at").notNull(),
  },
  (t) => [check("copy_marks_place", sql`${t.place} > 0`), fullAccess("copy_marks_api_all", apiRole)],
).enableRLS();
```

```ts
/**
 * The test adapters' fixtures (3d design, sections 5 "The adapters" and 12; Task 6 for the marker, Task 7 for the
 * matcher's files). The repository carries no image file and commits none: every image the suites use is encoded when
 * the test runs, and an encoder's bytes differ between machines, so what a test adapter recognises is written here as a
 * constant.
 *
 * The test scorer's marker (R1_CLASSIFIER=test): a block of one exact colour in the image's top left corner, at least
 * `side` pixels on each side. The scorer answers 1 for an image whose small size carries it, read from the raw sRGB
 * pixels the pipeline already holds, and 0 for every other image. It looks at the `probe` pixels on each side of the
 * corner and allows each channel `tolerance` levels, so the block survives the pipeline's resize and its conversion to
 * sRGB, and a lossy source's few levels of noise: a test proves it through the real pipeline.
 */
export const R1_MARKER = {
  red: 255,
  green: 0,
  blue: 255,
  /** The block's side in the uploaded image, in pixels: at least this much. */
  side: 64,
  /** The pixels on each side of the small size's corner that the scorer reads. */
  probe: 16,
  /** How far each channel may stray from the colour. */
  tolerance: 12,
} as const;

/**
 * Whether raw pixels (rows of `width` pixels of `channels` bytes, red first) carry the marker in their top left corner:
 * every pixel of the probe's square within the tolerance of the marker's colour. Too small an image carries none.
 */
export function carriesR1Marker(pixels: Uint8Array, width: number, height: number, channels: number): boolean {
  const { probe, tolerance } = R1_MARKER;
  if (channels < 3 || width < probe || height < probe || pixels.length < width * height * channels) return false;
  for (let y = 0; y < probe; y++) {
    for (let x = 0; x < probe; x++) {
      const at = (y * width + x) * channels;
      if (Math.abs(pixels[at]! - R1_MARKER.red) > tolerance || Math.abs(pixels[at + 1]! - R1_MARKER.green) > tolerance || Math.abs(pixels[at + 2]! - R1_MARKER.blue) > tolerance) return false;
    }
  }
  return true;
}

/**
 * The test matcher's two files (3d design, sections 5 "The adapters" and 12; Task 7, MEDIA_MATCH=test): two PNG images of
 * 8 by 8 pixels of one flat colour each, written out byte for byte as hexadecimal constants, so their digests are the same
 * on every machine and no encoder runs at test time. Each is the PNG signature, its IHDR chunk (8 by 8, 8-bit RGB), one
 * IDAT chunk holding a zlib stream with one stored (uncompressed) block of the eight rows (a filter byte of 0, then eight
 * pixels), and the IEND chunk; every CRC-32 and the Adler-32 are written out too. They show nothing: two flat colours.
 * The test adapter answers on their digests, computed from these bytes when it is built, and a unit test holds those to
 * node:crypto's. `acting` is the file the test matcher reports as an exact match of its listed and acting class;
 * `flag` is the one it reports as a match that does not act (near of the listed class, or of the class that is not
 * listed, as the test sets).
 */
const PNG_SIGNATURE = "89504e470d0a1a0a";
const PNG_IHDR_8X8_RGB = "0000000d49484452000000080000000808020000004b6d29dc";
const PNG_IEND = "0000000049454e44ae426082";

/** One fixture's hexadecimal bytes: the signature, IHDR, the IDAT chunk of eight equal rows, and IEND. */
function flatPng(row: string, adler: string, idatCrc: string): string {
  // The IDAT chunk: its length (211 bytes), its type, the zlib header and the stored block's header (final, 200 bytes),
  // the rows, the Adler-32 of the rows, and the chunk's CRC-32.
  return PNG_SIGNATURE + PNG_IHDR_8X8_RGB + "000000d3" + "49444154" + "780101c80037ff" + row.repeat(8) + adler + idatCrc + PNG_IEND;
}

/** Hexadecimal text as bytes. */
function bytesOf(hex: string): Uint8Array {
  const out = new Uint8Array(hex.length / 2);
  for (let i = 0; i < out.length; i++) out[i] = Number.parseInt(hex.slice(i * 2, i * 2 + 2), 16);
  return out;
}

export const MATCH_FIXTURES = {
  /** Flat 0x2060a0. */
  acting: bytesOf(flatPng("002060a02060a02060a02060a02060a02060a02060a02060a0", "026c4801", "e0c8ad94")),
  /** Flat 0xa06020. */
  flag: bytesOf(flatPng("00a06020a06020a06020a06020a06020a06020a06020a06020", "426c4801", "10978b5e")),
} as const;
```

```ts
 * The public rulebook. korbat restricts content when it breaks one of these rules, or when it is illegal under EU law or

/** The version a decision made now records. */
export const RULES_VERSION = 3;

/** Every version of the rulebook, by its number. */
export const RULEBOOKS = { 1: RULES_V1, 2: RULES_V2, 3: RULES_V3 } as const satisfies Record<number, readonly Rule[]>;

/** The rules in force. */
export const RULES = RULEBOOKS[RULES_VERSION];

/** One version of the rulebook as the rules page's change log prints it: the day it came into force and what it changed. */
export interface RulesChange {
  version: number;
  /** The day the version came into force, as the pages print a day. */
  date: string;
  summary: string;
}

/**
 * The rulebook's change log (3d design, sections 2 row 7, 9.2 and 10.8; W.1), oldest first: one dated sentence a version.
 * The day is a literal written by the task that ships the version; versions 1 to 3 carry the day of the commit that added
 * each to this file. The rules page prints it newest first.
 */
export const RULES_CHANGES: readonly RulesChange[] = [
  { version: 1, date: "2026-09-14", summary: "The six rules as first published." },
  {
    version: 2,
    date: "2026-10-04",
    summary:
      "A person decides every case; the automated checks that R1 and R2 named are withdrawn until they exist. R2 says how reported images are handled without anyone opening them. R4 and R5 say who may hide content while a case is decided and who decides it. R6 names coordinated manipulation.",
  },
  { version: 3, date: "2026-10-12", summary: "R6 names repeated, plainly unfounded reporting." },
];

export type RuleId = (typeof RULES)[number]["id"];

/** A rule as one version of the rulebook words it: the current version unless told. Undefined for an id or a version that does not exist. */
export function getRule(id: string, version: number = RULES_VERSION): Rule | undefined {
  const book: readonly Rule[] | undefined = (RULEBOOKS as Record<number, readonly Rule[]>)[version];
  return book?.find((rule) => rule.id === id);
}

export function isRuleId(id: string): id is RuleId {
  return RULES.some((rule) => rule.id === id);
}

/** What a statement of reasons tells its author they can do about the decision. Which text applies follows from the decision's own kind and outcome. */
export interface RedressTexts {
  /** A final decision that restricts: korbat's appeal. `{deadline}` stands for the last day of the appeal, which the statement fills in. */
  appeal: string;
  /** A decision taken while korbat decides. */
  interim: string;
  /** Any other decision, which its author cannot appeal. */
  notAppealable: string;
  // Version 2 (3e design, section 18, W.3). Their numbers are literals of the version, held to STANDING_RULES by a table
  // test: a changed number is a new version, so an old statement keeps its own.
  /** After a strike's sentence: the prior warning of what strikes lead to. */
  strikeNext?: string;
  /** An announced suspension or termination: the reply before the start. */
  reply?: string;
  /** A suspension or termination taken at once: the reply while it runs. */
  replyAtOnce?: string;
  /** A kept answer to a reply. `{deadline}` stands for the last day of the appeal of the decision it keeps. */
  replyAnswered?: string;
  /** After a warning about reporting: what may follow it. */
  warnNext?: string;
  /** An announced measure: the appeal does not wait for the start. */
  appealNow?: string;
  /** Version 3 (3f design, W.2 and W.3): the notice of an authority's order, ORDER_NOTICE. */
  order?: typeof ORDER_NOTICE;
  /**
   * Version 4 (3d design, W.4): "Ask for a person" in the place of `interim`, on a decision without a decider: `askPerson`
   * for a program's withhold of an image, `askAdmin` for its seal of a post's images; and `uploadObject`, the objection to
   * a refused upload (Task 7's notice).
   */
  askPerson?: string;
  askAdmin?: string;
  uploadObject?: string;
}

/**
 * The version of the redress texts a decision made now records. 3d Task 6 (design, section 10.8; W.4): 4, since a
 * program's decision records the version whose askPerson it prints, so the version cannot wait for the rulebook's.
 */
export const REDRESS_VERSION = 4;

const OUTSIDE_KORBAT = "complain to the Digital Services Coordinator of the EU country where you live (Article 53 of the Digital Services Act).";

const REDRESS_V1 = {
  appeal: `You can appeal this decision once, free of charge, within six months of being told, until {deadline}: choose "Appeal" on this decision's screen under Settings, Cases. A moderator who took no part in the case reviews it. You can also go to court, or ${OUTSIDE_KORBAT}`,
  interim: `This applies while korbat decides, and ends with its decision. If korbat's decision restricts your post or profile, you can appeal it. You can also go to court, or ${OUTSIDE_KORBAT}`,
  notAppealable: `korbat's appeal does not apply to this decision. Where an earlier decision about this content still stands in part, its own screen in korbat says whether you can still appeal it. You can go to court, or ${OUTSIDE_KORBAT}`,
} as const;

/** Account sanctions (3e): six more texts beside version 1's three, which version 2 holds word for word. */
const REDRESS_V2 = {
  strikeNext:
    "A strike restricts nothing by itself. When an account has 3 active strikes, a moderator may decide to suspend it for a limited time or, after three suspensions in 365 days, an admin may decide to terminate it. You would be told first and could reply before anything is restricted.",
  reply: `Before it starts you can reply: choose "Reply" on this decision's screen under Settings, Cases, and say anything you want the moderator to weigh. A reply sent before the start holds the start until a moderator has read it and answered you; if the decision is kept, it then starts with the answer, and never before the time you were given. A reply sent later is read and answered too, and can end this measure, but does not pause it. You can reply once. Replying does not use up your appeal.`,
  replyAtOnce: `You can reply at any time while it runs: choose "Reply" on this decision's screen under Settings, Cases. A moderator reads your reply and answers you, and can end this measure at once; the reply does not pause it. You can reply once. Replying does not use up your appeal.`,
  replyAnswered: `This answer is not appealed by itself. The appeal is against the decision it keeps: once, free of charge, until {deadline}, with "Appeal" on that decision's screen under Settings, Cases. The six months for it count from this answer when you replied before the start, and otherwise from the day you were told of that decision. You can also go to court, or ${OUTSIDE_KORBAT}`,
  warnNext: "If 3 of the reports you send after this warning are marked that way while it counts, a moderator may restrict your reports under korbat's rules for up to 30 days.",
  appealNow: "You can appeal from now; you do not have to wait for the start. An appeal does not hold the start: only a reply sent before the start does.",
} as const;

/**
 * 3d (design, W.4): version 3's texts word for word, and three that join. Each number in them is a literal of this
 * version, held to AUTOMATION_RULES.objectionTargetHours by the package's table test: a changed target is a new version,
 * so an old statement keeps its own.
 */
const REDRESS_V4 = {
  askPerson: `You can ask for a person now: choose "Ask for a person" on this decision's screen under Settings, Cases, and write anything a person should know. You can send one message. korbat's target is that a moderator answers within 24 hours; the measure does not end by itself before a person has decided. A measure a program takes cannot be appealed as such: ask for a person instead. The moderator's decision can be appealed, if it restricts your post. You can also go to court, or ${OUTSIDE_KORBAT}`,
  askAdmin: `You can ask for a person now: choose "Ask for a person" on this decision's screen under Settings, Cases, and write anything a person should know. You can send one message. korbat's target is that an admin answers within 24 hours; the measure does not end by itself before a person has decided. A measure a program takes cannot be appealed as such: ask for a person instead. The admin's decision can be appealed, if it seals the images for good; an appeal of a seal waits until the authorities have assessed the images. You can also go to court, or ${OUTSIDE_KORBAT}`,
  uploadObject: `You can object, free of charge: choose "Object" on this screen and write anything the admin should know. You can send one message, at any time before the hold is lifted or korbat has released the file, also after an admin has decided to report it. An admin, not a program, decides what happens to the file. Nobody at korbat can accept the image, since nobody opens it. You can also go to court, or ${OUTSIDE_KORBAT}`,
} as const;

/** Every version of the redress texts, by its number, kept as the rulebooks are. */
export const REDRESS_TEXTS = {
  1: REDRESS_V1,
  2: { ...REDRESS_V1, ...REDRESS_V2 },
  /**
   * 3f (design, section 10.7; W.3): version 2's nine texts word for word, and the group `order`, the notice of an
   * authority's order (ORDER_NOTICE of the statement's module), so a notice reads under its own version.
   */
  3: { ...REDRESS_V1, ...REDRESS_V2, order: ORDER_NOTICE },
  /** 3d Task 6 (W.4): version 3's texts word for word, and the three of "Ask for a person" and the upload's objection. */
  4: { ...REDRESS_V1, ...REDRESS_V2, order: ORDER_NOTICE, ...REDRESS_V4 },
} as const satisfies Record<number, RedressTexts>;

/** The redress texts of one version. Undefined for a version that does not exist. */
export function getRedress(version: number): RedressTexts | undefined {
  return (REDRESS_TEXTS as Record<number, RedressTexts>)[version];
}

// The statement of reasons, rendered over the rulebooks and the redress texts above. The package exports only this file,
// so the app, the console and the API reach the statement through it.
export {
  IMAGE_LOST_NOTICE,
  ORDER_NOTICE,
  RELEASE_DAY_NOTICE,
  RELEASE_NOTICE,
  STATEMENT_WORDS,
  UPLOAD_NOTICE,
  releaseNoticeParagraphs,
  uploadNoticeParagraphs,
  retireEnd,
  statementParagraphs,
  type OrderNoticeExtras,
  type RetireEnd,
  type StatementInput,
} from "./statement";
```

```ts
/**
 * The statement of reasons (3c design, section 10), as one pure function of a decision's data: the author's screen, the
 * console's preview and the mail all render it with this, so what the moderator previews is what the author gets. It
 * reads nothing but its input: the rule's words come from the rulebook version the decision was made under and the
 * redress text from its redress version, and which redress text applies follows from the decision's own kind and
 * outcome, never from a later event, so a statement reads as it was sent whenever it is rendered.
 *
 * It carries the six elements of Article 17(3) of the Digital Services Act: what was restricted, where and for how long;
 * the facts, and whether the decision followed a notice or korbat's own finding; whether automated means were used; the
 * legal ground or the rule, with its explanation; and the redress.
 */
export type StatementInput = DecisionStatement;

/** A time as korbat's mails print it: the date and the minute in UTC, since the reader's zone is unknown. */
function utcMinute(at: string | Date): string {
  const iso = (typeof at === "string" ? new Date(at) : at).toISOString();
  return `${iso.slice(0, 10)} ${iso.slice(11, 16)} UTC`;
}

const FIELD_NAMES = { display_name: "display name", bio: "bio" } as const;
type Field = keyof typeof FIELD_NAMES;

/** The field a reset or its lifting is about, or null for any other kind. */
function fieldOf(kind: MeasureKind | ReversalKind): Field | null {
  const target = MEASURES[kind].target;
  return target === "display_name" || target === "bio" ? target : null;
}
```
